h_k = 0^k 1^{5-k},   0≤k≤5

the six monotone 0*1* words 00000,00001,00011,00111,01111,11111. The reciprocal 1^k0^{5-k} products are the products of the asymmetric crossover on the opposite strand; they are not part of the + strand F1 pool and therefore are not part of the F2 haplotype pool. This is the operative meaning of “sufficient asymmetry … recombination in only one orientation” and “considering only the arbitrarily positive strand”.

An F2 individual is therefore h_a/h_b with h_a , h_b in 0*1*. An F2→F3 + strand gamete is

r_k(a,b)= h_a[1:k] h_b[k+1:5] = 0^{a}1^{k-a}0^{b-k}1^{5-b}

with 0≤a≤k≤b≤5 up to the trivial monotone cases. Hence every F3 + strand chromosome is a monotone prefix glued to a monotone suffix, i.e. a 0*1*0*1* word with first allele 0 and last allele 1, and can contain at most one 1→0 step.

10=0: the six monotone words 0^a1^{5-a}, N0=6.

10=1 with the unique 1→0 at p, 1≤p≤4. The left p sites must be a monotone word ending in 1, 0^{a}1^{p-a} with 0≤a<p, p choices; the right 5-p sites must be a monotone word beginning in 0, 0^{c}1^{5-p-c} with 0≤c≤5-p, 5-p choices. So N_p = p(5-p). Summing,

N1 = Σ_{p=1}^4 p(5-p) = 4+6+6+4 = 20.

N_+ = N0+N1 = 6+20 = 26 distinct + strand chromatid sequences in F3. The set is the 0*1*0*1* words with a single 1→0, e.g. 01011,01001,01101,00101, etc., together with the six monotones. Words with two 1→0 steps such as 01010,10101 and their neighbours are not realizable as a cut of two 0*1* words with a fixed left-to-right orientation.

That is why the 30 count is a double counting of orientations. The 30 = 32-2 count is obtained by allowing the F2→F3 meiosis to draw from both the 0*1* and 1*0* monotone families on the + strand, i.e. by re-introducing the reciprocal products that the asymmetry removes from the + strand in the F1. With the orientation kept fixed the second recombination cannot create a second 1→0.

The strict interior-crossover 8-haplotype limit is the same picture with the artificial exclusion of the telomeric k=0,5 crossovers; allowing the usual telomeric crossovers the founders stay in the pool and the 26 count is the natural + strand F3 repertoire, 26^2 = 676 ordered and 26·27/2 = 351 unordered diploid genotypes.

2.text:
On the $+$ strand put the two inbred founders

$$A=0^{5}\qquad B=1^{5}$$

and with the strand asymmetry write a meiosis in the fixed left to
right orientation

$$R_{k}(X,Y)=X_{1:k}Y_{k+1:5},\qquad 1\le k\le 4 ,$$

the reciprocal product being on the $- $ strand.  An obligate
crossover is required in every gamete so $k=0,5$ is not allowed.

$F_{1}\to F_{2}$.

$F_{1}$ is $A/B$ so on the $+$ strand

$${\cal G}_{1}=R_{k}(A,B)=0^{k}1^{5-k},\qquad k=1,\dots ,4,
$$

i.e.

$01111,\;00111,\;00011,\;00001 ,$$

the four $0^{*}1^{*}$ one–break molecules.  $A$ and $B$ themselves are
never made by an obligate interior crossover and every $F_{2}$ $+$
strand chromosome starts with $0$ and ends with $1$.

$F_{2}\to F_{3}$.

An $F_{2}$ chromosome is $h_{p}=0^{p}1^{5-p}$ with $p\in\{1,2,3,4\}$.
For $h_{p},h_{q}\in{\cal G}_{1}$

$$R_{k}(h_{p},h_{q})=h_{p}[1:k]h_{q}[k+1:5] .$$

Hence

$R_{k}(h_{p},h_{q})_{1}=0,\qquad R_{k}(h_{p},h_{q})_{5}=1$

for every $p,q,k$, and for $p<k<q$

$$R_{k}(h_{p},h_{q})=0^{p}1^{k-p}0^{\,q-k}1^{5-q}.$$

In particular the three interior sites $2,3,4$ can be chosen
independently.  Up to the fixed orientation

$${\cal H}_{3}^{+}=\{0\,x_{2}x_{3}x_{4}\,1:\;x_{2},x_{3},x_{4}\in\{0,1\}\},$$

viz.

$00001,\;00011,\;00101,\;00111,\;
 01001,\;01011,\;01101,\;01111,$

$|{\cal H}_{3}^{+}|=2^{\,5-2}=2^{3}=8$ different $+$ strand chromatids.
The four $F_{2}$ molecules $01111,00111,00011,00001$ are retained and the
four genuinely new two–meiotic molecules are

$01011=(1,2,3),\;01001=(1,2,4),\;01101=(1,3,4),\;00101=(2,3,4)$.

The two founder molecules $00000$ and $11111$ can never be recovered
with an obligate interior crossover.

In diploid terms an $F_{3}$ autosome is an unordered pair
$\{h_{1},h_{2}\}\subset{\cal H}_{3}^{+}$.  There are

$N_{\rm ord}=8^{2}=64$ ordered and $N_{\rm unord}=\binom{8+1}{2}=36$
unordered diploid $+$ strand genotypes in the $F_{3}$,
the familiar $2^{\,n-2}$ positive–strand limit for two rounds of
obligate single–crossover meiosis with a fixed orientation.

Remark.  If the trivial telomeric crossovers $k=0,5$ are formally
admitted the $F_{1}$ pool becomes the six monotone $0^{a}1^{5-a}$ words
and the $F_{3}$ $+$ strand pool is the $0^{*}1^{*}0^{*}1^{*}$ set with
at most one $1\to0$.  That is $N_{0}=6$ monotone words and
$N_{1}=\sum_{p=1}^{4}p(5-p)=20$ words with a single $1\to0$, i.e.
$N_{+}=26$ $+$ strand haplotypes, $26^{2}=676$ ordered and
$26\cdot27/2=351$ unordered diploid $F_{3}$ autosomes, the usual
text-book $26$ haplotype count.  The $8$ haplotype, $36$ unordered
diploid genotype, count above is the strict obligate-interior,
fixed-orientation limit required by “exactly one locus per gamete”. ∎

3.text:
On the + strand write the two inbred founders as

$A=0^{5},\qquad B=1^{5}$

and with the strand asymmetry write a meiosis on the + strand as the
fixed left $\to$ right cut and paste

$R_{k}(X,Y)=X[1:k]Y[k+1:5],\qquad 1\le k\le4,$

the $k=0,5$ zero–crossover products being excluded by the
“exactly one locus per generation for every gamete’’ condition.
The reciprocal product lives on the $-$ strand and is not counted on
the arbitrarily chosen + strand.

$F_{1}=A/B$.  On the + strand

${\cal G}_{1}=\{R_{k}(A,B):1\le k\le4\}
        =\{0^{k}1^{5-k}\}_{k=1}^{4}
        =\{01111,00111,00011,00001\}$

is the whole $F_{1}\to F_{2}$ gamete pool.  In particular every $F_{2}$
chromosome starts with $0$ and ends with $1$ and the two founders
$00000,11111$ are lost by the obligate interior crossover.  Up to the
fixed orientation $|{\cal G}_{1}|=n-1=4$.

An $F_{2}$ individual is $h_{i}/h_{j}$ with $h_{i},h_{j}\in{\cal G}_{1}$,
$h_{i}=0^{a}1^{5-a},\,h_{j}=0^{b}1^{5-b}$, $a,b\in\{1,2,3,4\}$.  An
$F_{2}\to F_{3}$ gamete on the + strand is

$s_{k}=R_{k}(h_{i},h_{j})=h_{i}[1:k]h_{j}[k+1:5],\qquad 1\le k\le4.$

Hence $s_{1}=0$, $s_{5}=1$ for every $i,j,k$ and

$s_{k}=0^{a}1^{\,k-a}0^{\,b-k}1^{\,5-b}$  for $a<k<b$,

and $s_{k}\in{\cal G}_{1}$ otherwise.  The three interior sites
$2,3,4$ can therefore be chosen independently.  The attainable
positive–strand haplotype set is

${\cal H}_{3}^{+}=\{0x_{2}x_{3}x_{4}1:x_{2},x_{3},x_{4}\in\{0,1\}\}
      =\{00001,00011,00101,00111,01001,01011,01101,01111\}$,

$|{\cal H}_{3}^{+}|=2^{\,n-2}=2^{3}=8$ different + strand molecules.
The four $F_{2}$ molecules $01111,00111,00011,00001$ are retained and
the four genuinely new two–meiosis molecules are
$01011=R_{2}(01111,00111)$, $01001=R_{2}(01111,00001)$,
$01101=R_{3}(01111,00111)$, $00101=R_{3}(00111,00001)$.
The founder haplotypes $00000$ and $11111$ can never be recovered with
an obligate interior crossover.

In diploid terms an $F_{3}$ autosome is an unordered pair
$\{h_{1},h_{2}\}\subset{\cal H}_{3}^{+}$.  There are
$|{\cal H}_{3}^{+}|^{2}=64$ ordered and

$N_{u}=\binom{8+1}{2}=36$

unordered diploid $F_{3}$ autosomes on the chosen + strand, the
usual $2^{\,n-2}$ positive–strand limit for two rounds of obligate
single-crossover meiosis with a fixed left–to–right orientation.

Remark.  If the trivial telomeric crossovers $k=0,5$ are admitted as
formal zero-crossover gametes the $F_{1}$ pool becomes the six monotone
$0^{a}1^{5-a}$, $0\le a\le5$, and the $F_{3}$ + strand pool becomes the
$0^{*}1^{*}0^{*}1^{*}$ words with at most one $1\to0$ step,
$N_{0}=6$ monotone and $N_{1}=\sum_{p=1}^{4}p(5-p)=20$ words with one
$1\to0$, i.e. $26$ + strand haplotypes, $26^{2}=676$ ordered and
$26\cdot27/2=351$ unordered diploid genotypes, the familiar
$26$-haplotype textbook count.  The $8$-haplotype $36$-genotype count
above is the strict obligate interior $1\le k\le4$, fixed orientation
limit required by “exactly one locus per generation for every gamete’’.

4.text:
On the arbitrarily chosen $+$ strand put

$A=0^{5},\qquad B=1^{5}$,

and write a single left $\to$ right meiosis as

$R_{k}(X,Y)=X_{1:k}Y_{k+1:5},\qquad 1\le k\le 4$,

the reciprocal product being on the $-$ strand.  The obligate interior
crossover is required for every gamete, so the trivial $k=0,5$
products are not present on the $+$ strand.

$F_{1}\to F_{2}$.  $F_{1}=A/B$,

${\cal G}_{1}=R_{k}(A,B)=0^{k}1^{5-k},\qquad1\le k\le4, $

$ {\cal G}_{1}=\{01111,00111,00011,00001\}$,

$|{\cal G}_{1}|=n-1=4$.  In particular every $F_{2}$ chromosome starts
with $0$ and ends with $1$ and the two founder molecules $00000,11111$
are lost by the obligate interior crossover.  Up to the fixed
left$\to$right orientation this is the whole $F_{2}$ haplotype pool.

$F_{2}\to F_{3}$.  Let $h_{i}=0^{i}1^{5-i},\,h_{j}=0^{j}1^{5-j}$,
$i,j\in\{1,2,3,4\}$, be two $F_{2}$ homologues.  On the $+$ strand

$h_{3}=R_{k}(h_{i},h_{j})=h_{i}[1:k]h_{j}[k+1:5]$

satisfies $h_{3,1}=0$ and $h_{3,5}=1$ for every $i,j,k$.  With
$i<k<j$

$h_{3}=0^{i}1^{\,k-i}0^{\,j-k}1^{\,5-j},$

and with $k\le i$ or $k\ge j$ the product is recovered in ${\cal G}_{1}$.
Hence every $F_{3}$ $+$ strand molecule is

$0\,x_{2}\,x_{3}\,x_{4}\,1,\qquad x_{2},x_{3},x_{4}\in\{0,1\}$,

i.e.

${\cal H}_{3}=\{0x_{2}x_{3}x_{4}1\}$

$00001,00011,00101,00111,01001,01011,01101,01111$,

$|{\cal H}_{3}|=2^{\,n-2}=2^{3}=8$

distinct $+$ strand chromatids.  The four $F_{2}$ molecules are retained
and the four new two–meiotic molecules

$01011=R_{2}(01111,00111),\;01001=R_{2}(01111,00001),$
$01101=R_{3}(01111,00111),\;00101=R_{3}(00111,00001)$

are created in the $F_{2}\to F_{3}$ meiosis.  The founder molecules
$00000$ and $11111$ can never be recovered with an obligate interior
crossover.

In diploid terms an $F_{3}$ autosome is an unordered pair
$\{h_{a},h_{b}\}\subset{\cal H}_{3}$.  There are $8^{2}=64$ ordered
maternal/paternal pairs and

$N_{d}^{u}=\binom{8+1}{2}=36$

unordered diploid $F_{3}$ autosomes on the fixed $+$ strand, the
$2^{\,n-2}$ positive–strand limit for two rounds of obligate
single-crossover meiosis with a fixed orientation.  This is the $8$
haplotype, $36$ unordered diploid genotype, limit.  With the usual
textbook convention that the trivial telomeric crossovers $k=0,5$ are
formally admitted the $F_{1}$ pool becomes the six monotone
$0^{a}1^{5-a}$ words and the $F_{3}$ $+$ strand pool becomes the
$0^{*}1^{*}0^{*}1^{*}$ words with at most one $1\to0$, $N_{+}=6+
\sum_{p=1}^{4}p(5-p)=26$ haplotypes, $26^{2}=676$ ordered and
$26\cdot27/2=351$ unordered diploid genotypes, the familiar $26$
haplotype statement. ∎

9.text:
On the arbitrarily chosen + strand put the two inbred founders

$$A=0^{5},\qquad B=1^{5}$$

and put a meiosis with the stated left–to–right asymmetry on the + strand
as

$$R_{k}(X,Y)=X_{1:k}Y_{k+1:5},\qquad 1\le k\le 4 ,$$

the obligate interior crossover.  The reciprocal product is on the – 
strand and is not counted on the + strand that is being followed.

$F_{1}\to F_{2}$.  $F_{1}=A/B$ gives on the + strand

$${\cal G}_{1}=\{R_{k}(A,B)\}_{k=1}^{4}
       =\{0^{k}1^{5-k}\}_{k=1}^{4}
       =01111,00111,00011,00001 ,$$

four $0^{*}1^{*}$ molecules.  In particular every $F_{2}$ chromosome
starts $0$ and ends $1$ and the two founder molecules $00000,11111$
are never made as gametes under a genuine obligate interior crossover.
Hence every $F_{2}$ individual is $h_{a}/h_{b}$ with
$h_{a},h_{b}\in{\cal G}_{1}$.

$F_{2}\to F_{3}$.  Put $h_{a}=0^{a}1^{5-a},\;h_{b}=0^{b}1^{5-b}$,
$a,b\in\{1,2,3,4\}$.  On the + strand

$$R_{k}(h_{a},h_{b})=h_{a}[1:k]h_{b}[k+1:5],\qquad1\le k\le4,$$

so that

$$R_{k}(h_{a},h_{b})_{1}=0,\qquad R_{k}(h_{a},h_{b})_{5}=1
\;\;\forall a,b,k,$$

and the $F_{2}\to F_{3}$ product is $0x_{2}x_{3}x_{4}1$.  For
$a<k<b$

$$R_{k}(h_{a},h_{b})=0^{a}1^{\,k-a}0^{\,b-k}1^{\,5-b},$$

and for $k\le a$ or $k\ge b$ the product is again a member of
${\cal G}_{1}$.  Hence with the fixed left→right orientation

$${\cal H}_{3}^{+}=\{0x_{2}x_{3}x_{4}1:x_{2},x_{3},x_{4}\in\{0,1\}\}$$

is the whole + strand chromatid pool that can be carried by an $F_{3}$
chromosome.  In closed form

$${\cal H}_{3}^{+}=00001,00011,00101,00111,
                01001,01011,01101,01111,$$

the four $F_{2}$ $0^{*}1^{*}$ molecules
$01111,00111,00011,00001$ together with the four new two–meiotic
molecules $01011,01001,01101,00101$.  Thus

$$|{\cal H}_{3}^{+}|=2^{\,5-2}=2^{3}=8$$

different + strand haplotypes are attainable in the $F_{3}$, the first
and last SNP being frozen to $0$ and $1$.  The two parental sequences
$00000$ and $11111$ can never be recovered with an obligate $1\le k\le4$
crossover.

In diploid terms an $F_{3}$ autosome is an unordered pair
$\{h_{1},h_{2}\}\subset{\cal H}_{3}^{+}$.  There are $8^{2}=64$ ordered
maternal/paternal pairs and

$$N_{d}^{u}=\binom{8+1}{2}=36$$

unordered diploid $F_{3}$ autosomes on the chosen + strand.  This is the
$2^{n-2}$ positive-strand limit for two rounds of obligate single
crossover with a fixed orientation.

Remark.  If the trivial telomeric products $k=0,5$ are admitted formally
as “a crossover’’ the $F_{1}$ pool becomes the six monotone
$0^{a}1^{5-a}$, $0\le a\le5$, words and an $F_{3}$ + strand chromatid is
a $0^{*}1^{*}0^{*}1^{*}$ word with at most one $1\to0$.  That conventional
text-book relaxation gives $N_{0}=6$ monotone words and
$N_{1}=\sum_{p=1}^{4}p(5-p)=20$ words with a single $1\to0$, i.e.
$N_{+}=6+20=26$ + strand haplotypes, $26^{2}=676$ ordered and
$26\cdot27/2=351$ unordered diploid genotypes, the usual $26$ haplotype
$F_{3}$ count.  The $8$ haplotype $36$ unordered diploid count above is
the strict obligate-interior-crossover, fixed-orientation limit that
follows from “exactly one locus per generation for every gamete’’.

11.text:
On the arbitrarily chosen + strand put

$A=0^{5},\qquad B=1^{5}$ 

and write the fixed left $\to$ right cut and paste on the + strand as

$R_{k}(X,Y)=X_{1:k}Y_{k+1:5},\qquad 0\le k\le5$ ,

the reciprocal $Y_{1:k}X_{k+1:5}$ living on the $-$ strand and therefore
not counted on the + strand.  Up to the trivial $k=0,5$ telomeric
cross-overs a meiosis is obligate.

$F_{1}=A/B$.  On the + strand

${\cal H}_{1}=R_{k}(A,B)=0^{k}1^{5-k},\qquad0\le k\le5$,

is the whole $F_{2}$ haplotype pool.  The six monotone $0^{*}1^{*}$
words

$00000,00001,00011,00111,01111,11111 $

are the only $F_{2}$ + strand chromatids.  The $1^{k}0^{5-k}$ reciprocal
products are on the $-$ strand under the one orientation rule.

An $F_{2}$ individual is $h_{a}/h_{b}$ with $h_{a},h_{b}\in{\cal H}_{1}$.
An $F_{2}\to F_{3}$ + strand gamete is

$r_{k}(a,b)=h_{a}[1:k]h_{b}[k+1:5]=0^{a}1^{k-a}0^{\,b-k}1^{5-b},
\qquad0\le a\le k\le b\le5,$

i.e. a monotone $0^{*}1^{*}$ prefix glued to a monotone $0^{*}1^{*}$
suffix.  In particular an $F_{3}$ + strand word can contain at most one
$1\to0$ transition.

* $10=0$ : $0^{a}1^{5-a}$, $a=0\ldots5$.  $N_{0}=6$.
* $10=1$ with the unique $1\to0$ at $p$, $1\le p\le4$.  The left $p$
sites have to be $0^{*}1^{*}$ ending in $1$ – $p$ possibilities – and
the right $5-p$ sites have to be $0^{*}1^{*}$ beginning in $0$ – $5-p$
possibilities.  Hence $N_{p}=p(5-p)$ and

$N_{1}=\sum_{p=1}^{4}p(5-p)=4+6+6+4=20$.

Hence on the fixed + strand

$N_{+}(F_{3})=N_{0}+N_{1}=6+20=26$

different chromatid sequences are attainable in the $F_{3}$,

$0^{*}1^{*}\cup0^{*}1^{*}0^{*}1^{*}$,

the six monotone words above together with the twenty words with a
single $1\to0$.  The six binary words which contain two $1\to0$ steps,
e.g. $01010$, $10101$, are the $2^{5}-26=6$ words which cannot be
written as a monotone prefix + monotone suffix and are therefore
absent from the + strand with the one orientation rule.

In diploid terms the $26$ haplotypes can be paired.  There are
$26^{2}=676$ ordered and $26\cdot27/2=351$ unordered $F_{3}$ autosomal
genotypes on the chosen strand.  This is the usual $0^{*}1^{*}0^{*}1^{*}$
$F_{3}$ repertoire.

Remark.  If the obligate crossover is required to fall strictly
inside the five SNP block, $1\le k\le4$, the $F_{1}$ + strand pool is
$\{0^{k}1^{5-k}\}_{k=1}^{4}$ and the two founder molecules $00000,11111$
are lost.  Every $F_{3}$ + strand chromatid is then $0x_{2}x_{3}x_{4}1$,
$|{\cal H}_{3}^{+}|=2^{\,5-2}=2^{3}=8$,

$00001,00011,00101,00111,01001,01011,01101,01111$,

the four $F_{2}$ $0^{*}1^{*}$ molecules and the four new two-break
molecules $01011,01001,01101,00101$.  That is $8^{2}=64$ ordered and
$\binom{8+1}{2}=36$ unordered diploid $F_{3}$ autosomes on the + strand,
the familiar $2^{n-2}$ positive-strand limit for two rounds of
obligatory interior single-crossover meiosis with a fixed orientation.
The $26$ haplotype count above is the $k=0,5$–allowed, i.e. crossover
may fall outside the 5-SNP block, maximal + strand repertoire. ∎

8.text:
On the + strand put the two inbred founders

$P_{0}=0^{5},\qquad P_{1}=1^{5}$

and write the directed single crossover on the + strand as

$R_{k}(X,Y)=X_{1:k}Y_{k+1:5},\qquad 0\le k\le5 ,$

the trivial $k=0,5$ products being the gametes obtained when the
obligatory crossover falls telomeric to the five–SNP block.  The
reciprocal $Y_{1:k}X_{k+1:5}$ products live on the – strand and are not
seen on the chosen + strand.

$F_{1}\to F_{2}$.  $F_{1}=P_{0}/P_{1}$ gives on the + strand

${\cal H}_{2}= \{R_{k}(P_{0},P_{1})\}_{0\le k\le5}
      =\{0^{k}1^{5-k}\}_{0\le k\le5} $

the six monotone $0^{*}1^{*}$ words

$00000,00001,00011,00111,01111,11111$,

$|{\cal H}_{2}|=6$, the reciprocal $1^{k}0^{5-k}$ family being on the –
strand.  An $F_{2}$ individual is $h_{a}/h_{b}$ with
$h_{a},h_{b}\in{\cal H}_{2}$.

$F_{2}\to F_{3}$.  With $h_{a}=0^{a}1^{5-a}$, $h_{b}=0^{b}1^{5-b}$,

$r_{k}(a,b)=h_{a}[1:k]h_{b}[k+1:5]
        =0^{a}1^{\,k-a}0^{\,b-k}1^{\,5-b}, \qquad 0\le a\le k\le b\le5,$

up to the monotone cases $a=k$ or $b=k$.  Hence every $F_{3}$ + strand
chromatid is a monotone prefix glued to a monotone suffix, i.e. a
binary word of length $5$ with ${\rm 10}(s)\le 1$.  Writing
${\rm 10}(s)=\#\{i:s_{i}=1,s_{i+1}=0\}$,

* ${\rm 10}=0$ : $0^{a}1^{5-a}$, $a=0\ldots5$, $N_{0}=6$;
* ${\rm 10}=1$ with the unique $1\to0$ at $p$, $1\le p\le4$.
  The left $p$ sites must be a $0^{*}1^{*}$ word ending in $1$, $p$
  possibilities $0^{a}1^{p-a}$, $0\le a<p$, and the right $5-p$ sites a
  $0^{*}1^{*}$ word beginning in $0$, $5-p$ possibilities
  $0^{c}1^{5-p-c}$.  Hence $N_{p}=p(5-p)$.

$N_{1}=\sum_{p=1}^{4}p(5-p)=4+6+6+4=20$

words with a single $1\to0$.  In total

$N_{+}(F_{3})=N_{0}+N_{1}=6+20=26$

different + strand chromatid sequences are attainable, the six
$0^{*}1^{*}$ words and the twenty $0^{*}1^{*}0^{*}1^{*}$ words with one
$1\to0$ step.  The $26$ words are

$00000,00001,00011,00111,01111,11111$

together with the $20$ words $0^{a}1^{g}0^{h}1^{c}$, $a+g+h+c=5$,
$g,h\ge0$, e.g. $01011,01001,01101,00101$ etc.  In particular words
with two $1\to0$ steps, $01010,10101$, etc., are excluded by the fixed
left-to-right orientation.  The $26$ chromatids can be paired at random,
$26^{2}=676$ ordered and

$N_{d}^{\rm u}= \binom{26+1}{2}=351$

unordered diploid $F_{3}$ autosomes on the chosen + strand.

Remark.  With the usual textbook convention $1\le k\le4$, i.e. an
obligatory interior crossover, the $F_{1}$ + strand pool is
$\{0^{k}1^{5-k}\}_{1\le k\le4}$, the founders $00000,11111$ are lost and
every $F_{3}$ + strand chromatid is $0x_{2}x_{3}x_{4}1$.  There are
$2^{\,5-2}=2^{3}=8$ + strand haplotypes

$00001,00011,00101,00111,01001,01011,01101,01111$,

$8^{2}=64$ ordered and $\binom{8+1}{2}=36$ unordered diploid $F_{3}$
autosomes, the $2^{\,n-2}$ positive-strand limit.  The $26$–haplotype,
$351$–unordered-genotype count above is the $k=0\ldots5$ version with
trivial telomeric crossovers admitted, i.e. the ordinary obligate
single-crossover $F_{3}$ repertoire on a fixed strand. ∎

10.text:
On the arbitrarily chosen $+$ strand put

$$A=0^{5},\qquad B=1^{5}$$

and with the strand asymmetry write a meiosis on the $+$ strand as the
fixed left$\to$right cut and paste

$$R_{k}(X,Y)=X_{1:k}Y_{k+1:5},\qquad 1\le k\le 4,$$

the reciprocal product being on the $-$ strand.  A gamete is required
to carry a cut, so the trivial $k=0,5$ products are not made.

$F_{1}\to F_{2}$.  The $F_{1}$ is $A/B$ and on the $+$ strand

$${\cal G}_{1}=\{R_{k}(A,B):1\le k\le 4\}
       =\{0^{k}1^{5-k}:1\le k\le 4\}
       =\{01111,00111,00011,00001\}$$

is the whole $F_{1}$ gamete pool.  In particular every $F_{2}$
chromosome starts $0$ and ends $1$ and the two founders $00000$ and
$11111$ are lost by the obligate interior crossover.  Up to the fixed
orientation $|{\cal G}_{1}|=n-1=4$.

$F_{2}\to F_{3}$.  An $F_{2}$ individual is $h_{i}/h_{j}$ with
$h_{i},h_{j}\in{\cal G}_{1}$, $h_{i}=0^{i}1^{5-i}$, $h_{j}=0^{j}1^{5-j}$,
$i,j\in\{1,2,3,4\}$.  Its $F_{2}\to F_{3}$ $+$ strand gamete is

$$h_{i,j,k}=R_{k}(h_{i},h_{j})=h_{i}[1:k]h_{j}[k+1:5],\qquad1\le k\le4,$$

i.e.

$$R_{k}(h_{i},h_{j})=0^{i}1^{\,k-i}0^{\,j-k}1^{\,5-j}
\qquad 1\le i,j,k\le4,$$

so that

$$h_{i,j,k\,1}=0,\qquad h_{i,j,k\,5}=1\qquad\forall i,j,k,$$

and the three interior sites $2,3,4$ can be chosen independently.
Hence, up to the fixed left$\to$right orientation,

$${\cal H}_{3}^{+}=\{0x_{2}x_{3}x_{4}1:x_{2},x_{3},x_{4}\in\{0,1\}\}$$

is the whole $+$ strand chromatid pool that can be carried by an $F_{3}$
chromosome.  In explicit form

$$\begin{aligned}
{\cal H}_{3}^{+}=&
00001,00011,00101,00111,\\
&01001,01011,01101,01111,
\end{aligned}$$

$|{\cal H}_{3}^{+}|=2^{\,5-2}=2^{3}=8$ different $+$ strand haplotypes.
The four $F_{2}$ molecules $01111,00111,00011,00001$ are retained and
the four genuinely new two-meiotic mosaics are

$01011=R_{2}(01111,00111),\;01001=R_{2}(01111,00001),$
$01101=R_{3}(01111,00111),\;00101=R_{3}(00111,00001)$,

the two founder molecules $00000$ and $11111$ never being recovered
with an obligate interior crossover.

In diploid terms an $F_{3}$ autosome is an unordered pair
$\{h_{1},h_{2}\}\subset{\cal H}_{3}^{+}$.  There are

$$N_{\rm ord}=|{\cal H}_{3}^{+}|^{2}=8^{2}=64$$

ordered maternal/paternal pairs and

$$N_{\rm u}=\binom{8+1}{2}=36$$

unordered diploid $F_{3}$ $+$ strand autosomes, the familiar
$2^{\,n-2}$ positive-strand limit for two rounds of obligate
single-crossover meiosis with a fixed orientation.  This is the strict
obligate interior $1\le k\le4$ limit.

Remark.  If the usual textbook convention that the trivial terminal
crossovers $k=0,5$ are formally admitted is used, the $F_{1}$ pool
becomes the six monotone $0^{a}1^{5-a}$, $0\le a\le5$, words and an
$F_{3}$ $+$ strand gamete is a $0^{*}1^{*}0^{*}1^{*}$ word with at most
one $1\to0$ step.  Then $N_{0}=6$ monotone words and
$N_{1}=\sum_{p=1}^{4}p(5-p)=20$ words with a single $1\to0$, i.e.
$N_{+}=6+20=26$ distinct $+$ strand haplotypes, $26^{2}=676$ ordered
and $26\cdot27/2=351$ unordered diploid $F_{3}$ genotypes, the
conventional $26$ haplotype $0^{*}1^{*}0^{*}1^{*}$ count. ∎

6.text:
On the arbitrarily chosen + strand put $A=0^{5}$ and $B=1^{5}$ and
write a fixed orientation meiosis as
$R_{k}(X,Y)=X_{1:k}Y_{k+1:5}.$
With an obligate internal cross $1\le k\le4$ the $F_{1}$ $+$ strand
gamete pool is

${\cal G}_{1}=R_{k}(A,B)=0^{k}1^{5-k},\qquad k=1\ldots 4,$

$01111,00111,00011,00001$, the four $0^{*}1^{*}$ molecules.  The two
founders $00000,11111$ are lost by the obligate internal cross and every
$F_{2}$ chromosome starts $0$ and ends $1$.

Let $h_{a}=0^{a}1^{5-a}$, $h_{b}=0^{b}1^{5-b}$ with $a,b\in\{1,2,3,4\}$.
An $F_{2}\to F_{3}$ + strand gamete is

$R_{k}(h_{a},h_{b})=0^{a}1^{k-a}0^{b-k}1^{5-b},\qquad 1\le a,k,b\le 4,$

so that $R_{k}(h_{a},h_{b})_{1}=0$ and $R_{k}(h_{a},h_{b})_{5}=1$.
Hence every $F_{3}$ + strand chromatid is

$0\,x_{2}x_{3}x_{4}\,1,\qquad x_{2},x_{3},x_{4}\in\{0,1\}.$

Up to the fixed left$\to$right orientation

${\cal H}_{3}^{+}=\{0x_{2}x_{3}x_{4}1\}$

and

$${\cal H}_{3}^{+}=00001,00011,00101,00111,
01001,01011,01101,01111.$$

$|{\cal H}_{3}^{+}|=2^{\,5-2}=2^{3}=8$ different + strand molecules.
The four $F_{2}$ molecules $01111,00111,00011,00001$ are retained and
the four new two-break molecules are

$01011=R_{2}(01111,00111),\;01001=R_{2}(01111,00001),$
$01101=R_{3}(01111,00111),\;00101=R_{3}(00111,00001)$.

In diploid terms an $F_{3}$ autosome is an unordered pair
$\{h_{1},h_{2}\}\subset{\cal H}_{3}^{+}$.  There are $8^{2}=64$ ordered
and

$N_{d}^{u}=\binom{8+1}{2}=36$

unordered + strand diploid genotypes, the familiar $2^{\,n-2}$ 
positive-strand limit for two rounds of obligate single-crossover meiosis
with a fixed orientation.  The $00000$ and $11111$ founders can never be
recovered with a genuine $1\le k\le4$ obligate cross.

*Remark.*  If the trivial telomeric crossovers $k=0,5$ are formally
admitted the $F_{1}$ pool becomes the six monotone $0^{a}1^{5-a}$ words
and an $F_{3}$ + strand word is $0^{*}1^{*}0^{*}1^{*}$ with at most one
$1\to0$ step.  There are $N_{0}=6$ monotone words and
$N_{1}=\sum_{p=1}^{4}p(5-p)=20$ words with a single $10$, i.e.
$N_{+}=6+20=26$ distinct + strand haplotypes, $26^{2}=676$ ordered and
$26\cdot27/2=351$ unordered diploid $F_{3}$ autosomes, the usual
$0^{*}1^{*}0^{*}1^{*}$ $F_{3}$ repertoire.

I’m with the orientation-restricted 0*1*0*1* count that Colleagues 1,5,6,7,8,11,12 are laying out.

Write the founders on the arbitrarily chosen + strand as A=00000, B=11111. With sufficient strand asymmetry a single meiosis is seen on the + strand only as

R_k(X,Y)=X[1:k]Y[k+1:5] ,

left block always from the first homologue. On A/B the F1 gametes that can be recorded on the + strand are therefore

h_k =0^k1^{5-k}, 0≤k≤5,

00000,00001,00011,00111,01111,11111.

The reciprocal 1^k0^{5-k} products live on the opposite strand and are not part of the + strand F1 pool. That is the whole F2 haplotype pool.

An F2 individual is h_a/h_b with h_a,h_b in 0*1*. An F2→F3 + strand gamete is

r_k(a,b)=h_a[1:k]h_b[k+1:5]=0^{a}1^{k-a}0^{b-k}1^{5-b}, 0≤a≤k≤b≤5,

up to the trivial monotone cases. Hence every F3 + strand word is a monotone prefix glued to a monotone suffix, i.e. 0*1*0*1* with at most one 1→0 step.

10=0: the six monotone words 0^a1^{5-a}, N0=6.

10=1 with the unique 1→0 at position p,1≤p≤4. The left p sites must be 0*1* ending in 1, p choices 0^{a}1^{p-a} with 0≤a<p, and the right 5-p sites must be 0*1* beginning in 0, 5-p choices 0^{c}1^{5-p-c}. So

N_p = p(5-p) , Σ_{p=1}^{4} p(5-p)=4+6+6+4=20.

Hence

N_+(F3)=6+20=26

different + strand chromatids are attainable, the six 0*1* words together with the twenty words with a single 1→0.

That is why words with two 1→0 steps such as 01010,10101 and the four near-alternating neighbours are absent on the fixed + strand. They would require a 1*0* monotone block to be spliced in at the F2→F3 meiosis, i.e. the reciprocal orientation that the strand asymmetry removes from the + strand.

The 30-haplotype construction re-introduces that reciprocal product at the second meiosis by letting the F2 parents be drawn from the full monotone set in both orientations. With the one-orientation rule the F2 pool is strictly 0*1*, so the second recombination cannot create a second 1→0. The strict interior-crossover 8-haplotype version is the same idea with the additional, unnecessary convention k∈{1..4} that discards the terminal crossovers k=0,5. Allowing the terminal loci as the statement “exactly one locus per generation for every gamete” permits gives the 26 haplotypes, i.e. 26² ordered and 26·27/2=351 unordered diploid F3 autosomes on the chosen + strand.

The + strand convention is the whole story.

Put the founders on the + strand as A=00000 and B=11111. With the stated strand asymmetry a meiosis is on the + strand the left-to-right cut-and-paste

R_k(X,Y)=X[1:k] Y[k+1:5] ,

and it is obligate, one cut per gamete. On the A/B heterozygote

R_k(A,B)=0^k1^{5-k}, 0 ≤ k ≤ 5,

the six monotone 0*1* words. The 1^k0^{5-k} reciprocal products live on the opposite strand and are not part of the + strand F1 pool. Hence the whole F2 pool is

H2 = {0^a1^{5-a} : 0≤a≤5} , |H2|=6,

the usual 0*1* set, with the two founders included as the k=0,5 trivial cuts.

r_k(a,b)=h_a[1:k] h_b[k+1:5]=0^a1^{k-a}0^{b-k}1^{5-b}, 0≤a≤k≤b≤5,

up to relabelling. That is a monotone prefix glued to a monotone suffix, i.e. a binary word of length 5 with at most one 1→0 step. A second fixed-orientation cut of two 0*1* haplotypes can create at most one 1→0, never two.

Count them on the + strand.

10=0 : the six monotone 0^a1^{5-a}, N0=6.

10=1 with the unique 1→0 at p,1≤p≤4. The left p sites must be 0*1* ending in 1, 0^a1^{p-a} with 0≤a<p, p choices. The right 5-p sites must be 0*1* beginning in 0, 0^c1^{5-p-c} with 0≤c≤5-p, 5-p choices. So N_p = p(5-p). 

N1 = Σ_{p=1}^{4} p(5-p)=4+6+6+4=20.

N+ =6+20=26 distinct + strand chromatids in F3, the six 0*1* words together with the twenty 0*1*0*1* words with a single 1→0. That is 351 unordered diploid autosomes.

That is why 01010,10101 and the four words that need two 1→0 steps never appear on the fixed + strand. They would require a 1*0* block to be spliced in at the second meiosis, i.e. the reciprocal orientation of the asymmetric crossover to be re-introduced on the + strand in F2→F3. The 30 haplotype count is exactly the count you get when you allow both orientations per meiosis, i.e. when you let the F2 pool be 0*1* ∪1*0*. With the one-orientation rule the F2 pool is strictly 0*1* and the second recombination cannot create a second 1→0.

I agree with the 26-haplotype accounting once the fixed left-to-right rule on the arbitrarily chosen + strand is kept consistent across the two meioses.

Write the two inbred founders on the + strand as P0 = 00000 and P1 = 11111. With the stated strand asymmetry a meiosis is seen on the + strand only as

R_k(X,Y)= X[1:k] Y[k+1:5]

with the left block always taken from the first homologue. On the F1 heterozygote P0/P1 this gives on the + strand

h_k = 0^k 1^{5-k},   0≤k≤5

the six monotone 0*1* words 00000,00001,00011,00111,01111,11111. The reciprocal 1^k0^{5-k} products are the products of the asymmetric crossover on the opposite strand; they are not part of the + strand F1 pool and therefore are not part of the F2 haplotype pool. This is the operative meaning of “sufficient asymmetry … recombination in only one orientation” and “considering only the arbitrarily positive strand”.

An F2 individual is therefore h_a/h_b with h_a , h_b in 0*1*. An F2→F3 + strand gamete is

r_k(a,b)= h_a[1:k] h_b[k+1:5] = 0^{a}1^{k-a}0^{b-k}1^{5-b}

with 0≤a≤k≤b≤5 up to the trivial monotone cases. Hence every F3 + strand chromosome is a monotone prefix glued to a monotone suffix, i.e. a 0*1*0*1* word with first allele 0 and last allele 1, and can contain at most one 1→0 step.

10=0: the six monotone words 0^a1^{5-a}, N0=6.

10=1 with the unique 1→0 at p, 1≤p≤4. The left p sites must be a monotone word ending in 1, 0^{a}1^{p-a} with 0≤a<p, p choices; the right 5-p sites must be a monotone word beginning in 0, 0^{c}1^{5-p-c} with 0≤c≤5-p, 5-p choices. So N_p = p(5-p). Summing,

N1 = Σ_{p=1}^4 p(5-p) = 4+6+6+4 = 20.

N_+ = N0+N1 = 6+20 = 26 distinct + strand chromatid sequences in F3. The set is the 0*1*0*1* words with a single 1→0, e.g. 01011,01001,01101,00101, etc., together with the six monotones. Words with two 1→0 steps such as 01010,10101 and their neighbours are not realizable as a cut of two 0*1* words with a fixed left-to-right orientation.

That is why the 30 count is a double counting of orientations. The 30 = 32-2 count is obtained by allowing the F2→F3 meiosis to draw from both the 0*1* and 1*0* monotone families on the + strand, i.e. by re-introducing the reciprocal products that the asymmetry removes from the + strand in the F1. With the orientation kept fixed the second recombination cannot create a second 1→0.

The strict interior-crossover 8-haplotype limit is the same picture with the artificial exclusion of the telomeric k=0,5 crossovers; allowing the usual telomeric crossovers the founders stay in the pool and the 26 count is the natural + strand F3 repertoire, 26^2 = 676 ordered and 26·27/2 = 351 unordered diploid genotypes.

$00001,00011,00101,00111,01001,01011,01101,01111$,

The founders on the arbitrarily chosen + strand are A=00000, B=11111. With strand asymmetry a meiosis on the + strand is the fixed left-to-right cut-and-paste R_k(X,Y)=X[1:k]Y[k+1:5]. 

F1→F2.  With the asymmetry the F1 gamete pool on the + strand is the monotone 0*1* family. If the obligate crossover is required to fall strictly inside the 5-SNP block, 1≤k≤4, the F1→F2 + strand pool is
{01111,00111,00011,00001}, |H1+|=4, and the two founders 00000,11111 are lost. If the trivial telomeric crossovers k=0,5 are admitted as the “one locus per generation’’ outside the block, the F1→F2 + strand pool is the six monotone words
0^k1^{5-k}, 0≤k≤5,
{00000,00001,00011,00111,01111,11111}, |H2+|=6. The reciprocal 1^k0^{5-k} products live on the – strand.

F2→F3.  An F2 individual is h_a/h_b with h_a,h_b in the monotone family. On the + strand
r_k(a,b)=h_a[1:k]h_b[k+1:5]=0^a1^{k-a}0^{b-k}1^{5-b}, 0≤a≤k≤b≤5,
i.e. a monotone prefix glued to a monotone suffix. Hence every F3 + strand word is 0*1*0*1* with at most one 1→0 step, first allele 0 and last allele 1 in the interior-crossover limit.

Strict interior 1≤k≤4 limit:
Every F3 + strand chromatid is 0 x2 x3 x4 1. 
H3+ = {0 x2 x3 x4 1 : x2,x3,x4∈{0,1}} = 
00001,00011,00101,00111,01001,01011,01101,01111,
|H3+|=2^{5-2}=8 haplotypes. Four are the F2 molecules, four are the new two-meiotic mosaics 01011,01001,01101,00101. The founders 00000,11111 are never recovered. Diploid + strand: 8²=64 ordered, C(8+1,2)=36 unordered autosomes.

Terminal-crossover admitted, i.e. the usual “one obligate crossover per meiosis’’ allowing the crossover to lie outside the block:
N0=6 monotone 0^a1^{5-a} words.
With a unique 1→0 at p,1≤p≤4, Np=p(5-p). 
N1=∑p(5-p)=4+6+6+4=20.
N+(F3)=N0+N1=6+20=26 distinct + strand haplotypes, the 0*1*0*1* set with ≤1 1→0. 
Diploid: 26²=676 ordered, 26·27/2=351 unordered genotypes. Words with two 1→0 steps e.g. 01010,10101 are absent on the fixed + strand.

The 30/22/8 counts arise from different counting conventions: 30=32-2 is the two-orientation / ≤3 switches count, 22=2∑_{k≤2}C(4,k) is the orientation-doubled ≤2-break count, 8 is the strict interior fixed-orientation positive-strand limit quoted as 2^{n-2}. The 26 haplotype, 351 unordered diploid genotype count is the conventional fixed-orientation F3 repertoire with k=0..5 admitted; the 8 haplotype, 36 unordered diploid genotype count is the same construction with the extra interior k=1..4 restriction that discards the founders. Unresolved is whether the problem intends the strict interior obligate crossover or the usual terminal-admitted obligate crossover.
reflection_text.10:

R_k(X,Y)=X[1:k]Y[k+1:5]. 
The question is whether the obligate crossover must be interior, 1≤k≤4, or whether the trivial telomeric cuts k=0,5 are formally admitted.

Strict interior, obligate 1≤k≤4, fixed orientation:

F1→F2 gametes on + strand are R_k(A,B)=0^k1^{5-k}, k=1..4,
G1={01111,00111,00011,00001}. |G1|=4. The founders 00000,11111 are lost by the obligate interior crossover and every F2 chromosome now starts 0 and ends 1.

F2→F3 gamete = R_k(X,Y) with X,Y∈G1, 1≤k≤4. Writing X=0^i1^{5-i}, Y=0^j1^{5-j},
R_k(X,Y)=0^i1^{k-i}0^{j-k}1^{5-j}. Hence R_k(X,Y)_1=0, R_k(X,Y)_5=1 for all i,j,k. The three interior sites 2,3,4 are free. 
H3+ = {0 x2 x3 x4 1 : x2,x3,x4∈{0,1}} = {00001,00011,00101,00111,01001,01011,01101,01111}, |H3+|=2^{5-2}=8 distinct + strand haplotypes.
The four F2 haplotypes are retained and the four new two-break mosaics are 01011,01001,01101,00101.
Diploid level: N_ord=8^2=64 ordered, N_unord=binom(8+1,2)=36 unordered + strand autosomes. This is the 2^{n-2} positive-strand limit for two rounds of obligate interior single-crossover meiosis with a fixed orientation.

Relaxed textbook convention admitting terminal crossovers k=0,5:

F1 pool becomes the six monotone 0*1* words h_a=0^a1^{5-a},0≤a≤5. An F2→F3 + strand gamete is h_a[1:k]h_b[k+1:5]=0^a1^{k-a}0^{b-k}1^{5-b}, i.e. a 0*1*0*1* word with at most one 1→0. Counting 10(s)=0 gives the six monotone words and 10(s)=1 at position p gives p(5-p) words. Σ p(5-p)=20. Hence N+ =6+20=26 + strand haplotypes, 26^2=676 ordered, 26·27/2=351 unordered diploid genotypes. This is the 0*1*0*1* count commonly quoted as 26.

Colleagues 2,3,4,6,9,10 argue for the strict interior k=1..4 version giving 8 + strand haplotypes, 36 unordered diploid autosomes, with the 26 count noted as the k=0,5 relaxation. The disagreement is exactly the telomeric vs strictly interior crossover convention and whether the count requested is haploid or diploid, and whether ordered vs unordered pairs are wanted. Unresolved is the interpretation of “exactly one locus per generation for every gamete” as prohibiting the trivial k=0,5 cuts; under the literal interior reading the F3 + strand haplotype repertoire is 8, and the autosomal diploid repertoire is 36 unordered, 64 ordered.

$$R_{k}(h_{i},h_{j})=h_{i}[1:k]h_{j}[k+1:5],\qquad 1\le k\le4, $$

i.e.

$$R_{k}(h_{i},h_{j})=0^{i}1^{\,k-i}0^{\,j-k}1^{\,5-j}, $$

so that

$$R_{k}(h_{i},h_{j})_{1}=0,\qquad R_{k}(h_{i},h_{j})_{5}=1\qquad\forall
i,j,k.$$

Hence every $F_{3}$ $+$ strand chromatid is of the form $0x_{2}x_{3}x_{4}1$.
With the fixed left$\to$right orientation the three interior sites are
independent.  Up to orientation

$${\cal H}_{3}^{+}=\{0x_{2}x_{3}x_{4}1:x_{2},x_{3},x_{4}\in\{0,1\}\},$$

explicitly

$$
\begin{aligned}
{\cal H}_{3}^{+}=&00001,00011,00101,00111,\\
                 &01001,01011,01101,01111,
\end{aligned}
$$

$|{\cal H}_{3}^{+}|=2^{\,5-2}=2^{3}=8$ different $+$ strand haplotypes.
The four $F_{2}$ molecules $01111,00111,00011,00001$ are retained and the
four genuinely new two–meiotic mosaics are

$01011=R_{2}(01111,00111),\;01001=R_{2}(01111,00001),$
$01101=R_{3}(01111,00111),\;00101=R_{3}(00111,00001),$

the founders $00000,11111$ never being recovered with an obligate
$1\le k\le4$ crossover.

In diploid terms an $F_{3}$ autosome is an unordered pair
$\{h_{1},h_{2}\}\subset{\cal H}_{3}^{+}$.  There are

$N_{\rm ord}=|{\cal H}_{3}^{+}|^{2}=8^{2}=64$

ordered maternal/paternal pairs and

$N_{u}=\binom{8+1}{2}=36$

unordered $+$ strand diploid $F_{3}$ autosomes, the familiar
$2^{\,n-2}$ positive-strand limit for two rounds of obligate interior
single-crossover meiosis with a fixed orientation.

Remark.  If the textbook convention $k=0,5$ is admitted as a formal
zero-recombination gamete the $F_{1}$ $+$ strand pool becomes the six
monotone $0^{a}1^{5-a}$, $0\le a\le5$, words.  An $F_{2}\to F_{3}$ $+$
strand gamete is then $h_{a}[1:k]h_{b}[k+1:5]=0^{a}1^{k-a}0^{b-k}1^{5-b}$,
i.e. a $0^{*}1^{*}0^{*}1^{*}$ word with at most one $1\to0$ step.
There are $N_{0}=6$ monotone words and $N_{p}=p(5-p)$ words with the
unique $1\to0$ at $p$, $N_{1}=\sum_{p=1}^{4}p(5-p)=20$, so that

$N_{+}(F_{3})=6+20=26$

distinct $+$ strand chromatids are attainable, $26^{2}=676$ ordered and
$26\cdot27/2=351$ unordered diploid $F_{3}$ genotypes on the chosen
strand.  This is the $0^{*}1^{*}0^{*}1^{*}$ $26$-haplotype count obtained
when the terminal $k=0,5$ crossovers are kept in the pool. ∎

11.text:
On the arbitrarily chosen $+$ strand write the two inbred founders as

$A=0^{5}=00000$ , $B=1^{5}=11111$

and with the strand asymmetry a meiosis on the $+$ strand is the fixed
left$\to$right cut and paste

$R_{k}(X,Y)=X_{1:k}Y_{k+1:5}$ , $0\le k\le5$,

the reciprocal $Y_{1:k}X_{k+1:5}$ being on the $-$ strand and therefore
not counted on the chosen strand.  Up to the usual formal terminal
$k=0,5$ cuts

${\cal H}_{1}^{+}=R_{k}(A,B)=0^{k}1^{\,5-k}$ , $0\le k\le5$,

i.e. the six monotone $0^{*}1^{*}$ words

$00000,00001,00011,00111,01111,11111$,

$|{\cal H}_{1}^{+}|=6$, the $1^{k}0^{5-k}$ reciprocals living on the $-$
strand.  This is the whole $F_{2}$ $+$ strand haplotype pool.

An $F_{2}$ individual is $h_{a}/h_{b}$ with $h_{a},h_{b}\in{\cal H}_{1}^{+}$,
$h_{a}=0^{a}1^{5-a}$, $h_{b}=0^{b}1^{5-b}$.  An $F_{2}\to F_{3}$ $+$ strand
gamete is

$r_{k}(a,b)=h_{a}[1:k]h_{b}[k+1:5]
        =0^{a}1^{\,k-a}0^{\,b-k}1^{\,5-b}$ , $0\le a\le k\le b\le5$,

i.e. a monotone $0^{*}1^{*}$ prefix glued to a monotone $0^{*}1^{*}$
suffix.  In particular every $F_{3}$ $+$ strand word can contain at most
one $1\to0$ transition.

$10=0$ : $0^{a}1^{5-a}$, $a=0\ldots5$, $N_{0}=6$.

$10=1$ with the unique $1\to0$ at $p$, $1\le p\le4$.  The left $p$ sites
have to be a $0^{*}1^{*}$ word ending in $1$, $p$ possibilities
$0^{a}1^{p-a}$, $0\le a<p$, and the right $5-p$ sites a $0^{*}1^{*}$ word
beginning in $0$, $5-p$ possibilities.  Hence $N_{p}=p(5-p)$ and

$N_{1}=\sum_{p=1}^{4}p(5-p)=4+6+6+4=20$.

Hence on the fixed $+$ strand

$N_{+}(F_{3})=N_{0}+N_{1}=6+20=26$

different chromatid sequences are attainable, the six $0^{*}1^{*}$ words
together with the twenty $0^{*}1^{*}0^{*}1^{*}$ words with a single
$1\to0$.  The $26$ chromatids can be paired.  There are $26^{2}=676$
ordered maternal/paternal pairs and

$N_{d}^{u}=\binom{26+1}{2}=26\cdot27/2=351$

unordered diploid $F_{3}$ autosomes on the chosen strand.  The six
binary words with two $1\to0$ steps, e.g. $01010$, are the
$2^{5}-26=6$ words which cannot be written as a monotone prefix $+$
monotone suffix and are absent from the $+$ strand with the one
orientation rule.

Remark.  With the strict obligate interior convention $1\le k\le4$
the terminal $k=0,5$ products are removed.  Then
${\cal G}_{1}^{+}=\{0^{k}1^{5-k}\}_{k=1}^{4}$, the founders $00000$,
$11111$ are lost and every $F_{3}$ $+$ strand chromatid is
$0x_{2}x_{3}x_{4}1$.  Hence $|{\cal H}_{3}^{+}|=2^{5-2}=2^{3}=8$,

$00001,00011,00101,00111,01001,01011,01101,01111$,

$8^{2}=64$ ordered and $\binom{8+1}{2}=36$ unordered diploid $F_{3}$
$+$ strand autosomes, the familiar $2^{\,n-2}$ positive-strand limit for
two rounds of obligate interior single-crossover meiosis with a fixed
orientation.  The $26$ haplotype, $351$ unordered diploid genotype,
count above is the $k=0\ldots5$ conventional $0^{*}1^{*}0^{*}1^{*}$ $F_{3}$
repertoire. ∎

2.text:
On the $+$ strand write the two inbred founders as

$$A=0^{5},\qquad B=1^{5}$$

and with the stated strand asymmetry write a meiosis on the $+$
strand as the fixed left $\to$ right cut and paste

$$R_{k}(X,Y)=X_{1:k}Y_{k+1:5}\;,$$

the reciprocal $Y_{1:k}X_{k+1:5}$ being on the $-$ strand and therefore
not counted on the chosen strand.  With an obligate interior cross the
gamete pool produced by $A/B$ on the $+$ strand is

$${\cal G}_{1}=R_{k}(A,B)=0^{k}1^{5-k},\qquad 1\le k\le 4,$$

i.e.

$$01111,\;00111,\;00011,\;00001,$$

$|{\cal G}_{1}|=n-1=4$ monotone $0^{*}1^{*}$ molecules.  In particular
every $F_{2}$ $+$ strand chromosome starts $0$ and ends $1$ and the two
founder molecules $00000$ and $11111$ are lost by the obligate interior
crossover.  Up to the fixed orientation this is the whole $F_{2}$
haplotype pool.

Let $h_{a}=0^{a}1^{5-a}$, $h_{b}=0^{b}1^{5-b}$ with $a,b\in\{1,2,3,4\}$
be two $F_{2}$ homologues.  An $F_{2}\to F_{3}$ $+$ strand gamete is

$$R_{k}(h_{a},h_{b})=h_{a}[1:k]h_{b}[k+1:5]
      =0^{a}1^{\,k-a}0^{\,b-k}1^{\,5-b},\qquad1\le k\le4,$$

so that

$$R_{k}(h_{a},h_{b})_{1}=0,\qquad R_{k}(h_{a},h_{b})_{5}=1
\;\;\forall\,a,b,k,$$

and with $a<k<b$

$$R_{k}(h_{a},h_{b})=0^{a}1^{k-a}0^{b-k}1^{5-b}.$$

Hence every $F_{3}$ $+$ strand chromatid is of the form $0x_{2}x_{3}x_{4}1$,
the three interior sites being free.  Up to the fixed left $\to$ right
orientation

$${\cal H}_{3}^{+}=\{0x_{2}x_{3}x_{4}1:x_{2},x_{3},x_{4}\in\{0,1\}\}$$

viz.

$$
\begin{array}{llll}
00001,&00011,&00101,&00111,\\
01001,&01011,&01101,&01111,
\end{array}
$$

$|{\cal H}_{3}^{+}|=2^{\,5-2}=2^{3}=8$ different $+$ strand
haplotypes.  The four $F_{2}$ molecules $01111,00111,00011,00001$ are
retained and the four genuinely new two-meiotic mosaics are

$01011=R_{2}(01111,00111),\;01001=R_{2}(01111,00001),$
$01101=R_{3}(01111,00111),\;00101=R_{3}(00111,00001),$

the founder molecules $00000$ and $11111$ never being recoverable with
an obligate $1\le k\le4$ cross.  This is the familiar $2^{\,n-2}$
positive-strand limit for two rounds of obligate single-crossover
meiosis with a fixed orientation.

In diploid terms an $F_{3}$ autosome is an unordered pair
$\{h_{1},h_{2}\}\subset{\cal H}_{3}^{+}$.  There are

$$N_{\rm ord}=|{\cal H}_{3}^{+}|^{2}=8^{2}=64$$

ordered maternal/paternal pairs and

$$N_{\rm u}=\binom{8+1}{2}=36$$

unordered diploid $F_{3}$ $+$ strand autosomes, the $2^{\,n-2}$ 
positive-strand limit.  The $8$ haplotypes are the $0^{*}1^{*}0^{*}1^{*}$
words with the first and last SNP frozen to $0$ and $1$, i.e. at most one
$1\to0$ step on the fixed $+$ strand.

Remark.  If the trivial telomeric cuts $k=0,5$ are formally admitted as
“a crossover’’ the $F_{1}$ $+$ strand pool becomes the six monotone
$0^{a}1^{5-a}$, $0\le a\le5$, words and an $F_{3}$ $+$ strand word is a
$0^{*}1^{*}0^{*}1^{*}$ word with at most one $1\to0$.  Then
$N_{0}=6$ monotone words and $N_{1}=\sum_{p=1}^{4}p(5-p)=20$ words with a
single $1\to0$, i.e. $N_{+}(F_{3})=6+20=26$ distinct $+$ strand
chromatids, $26^{2}=676$ ordered and $26\cdot27/2=351$ unordered
diploid $F_{3}$ autosomes on the chosen strand, the usual
$0^{*}1^{*}0^{*}1^{*}$ textbook repertoire.  The $8$-haplotype,
$36$-unordered-diploid count above is the strict obligate-interior
$1\le k\le4$ fixed-orientation limit. ∎

7.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: The + strand convention is decisive and it has to be kept the same in the two meioses.

Put the founders on the chosen + strand as

A = 0⁵ ,  B = 1⁵

and with the stated strand asymmetry write a meiosis on the + strand as the fixed left→right cut and paste

R_k(X,Y)=X[1:k]Y[k+1:5] ,  0 ≤ k ≤ 5 ,

the reciprocal Y[1:k]X[k+1:5] living on the – strand.  The wording
“exactly one locus per generation for every gamete’’ does not force the
locus to fall inside the five SNP interval.  A telomeric cut k=0,5 is still
exactly one crossover per gamete, it is simply telomeric to the block,
and it is the normal textbook way of keeping the founders in the gamete
pool.  With that usual reading

R_k(A,B)=0ᵏ1^{5−k}=h_k ,  0≤k≤5,

so on the + strand

H₂ = {0ᵏ1^{5−k}:0≤k≤5}=00000,00001,00011,00111,01111,11111

is the whole F₁→F₂ gamete pool, |H₂|=6 monotone 0*1* words.  The
1ᵏ0^{5−k} reciprocal products are on the – strand and are therefore not
part of the + strand F₂ pool.  Every F₂ chromosome is h_a/h_b with
h_a,h_b∈H₂.

An F₂→F₃ + strand gamete is

r_k(a,b)=h_a[1:k]h_b[k+1:5]=0^{a}1^{k−a}0^{b−k}1^{5−b},
0≤a≤k≤b≤5,

i.e. a monotone 0*1* prefix glued to a monotone 0*1* suffix.  In
particular an F₃ + strand word can contain at most one 1→0 step.  Let
10(s) be the number of 1→0 transitions.

10=0 : 0^{a}1^{5−a}, a=0…5.  N₀=6.

10=1 with the unique 1→0 at p, 1≤p≤4.  The left p sites have to be a
0*1* word ending in 1, 0^{a}1^{p−a} with 0≤a<p, p choices; the right
5−p sites have to be a 0*1* word beginning in 0, 0^{c}1^{5−p−c} with
0≤c≤5−p, 5−p choices.  Hence

N_p = p(5−p) ,  Σ_{p=1}^{4} p(5−p)=4+6+6+4=20.

Hence on the fixed + strand

N₊(F₃)=N₀+N₁=6+20=26

different chromatid sequences are attainable, the six 0*1* words together
with the twenty 0*1*0*1* words with a single 1→0, e.g.

01011=R₂(01111,00111), 01001=R₂(01111,00001),
01101=R₃(01111,00111), 00101=R₃(00111,00001),

etc.  Words with two 1→0 steps such as 01010,10101 and the four
near-alternating neighbours are absent on the fixed + strand.  They would
require a 1*0* monotone block to be spliced in at the F₂→F₃ meiosis,
i.e. the reciprocal orientation that the stated strand asymmetry removes
from the + strand in the second meiosis.  That is why the 30-haplotype
construction is a double counting of orientations: it re-introduces the
reciprocal 1*0* monotone family on the + strand at the second meiosis.

The strict interior 1≤k≤4 version is the same picture with the
artificial extra convention that a crossover must fall strictly inside the
five SNP block.  With 1≤k≤4 the founders 00000,11111 are lost in F₁ and
every F₃ + strand chromatid is 0x₂x₃x₄1, |H₃⁺|=2^{5−2}=8.  That is a
legitimate pedantic limit, but it is not required by “exactly one locus
per generation for every gamete’’.  Allowing the usual terminal
k=0,5 cuts the founders stay in the pool and the natural + strand F₃
repertoire is the 26 0*1*0*1* set, 26²=676 ordered and 26·27/2=351
unordered diploid F₃ autosomes on the chosen + strand.

On the arbitrarily chosen $+$ strand put the two inbred founders

$A=0^{5},\qquad B=1^{5}$

and write the directed meiosis on the $+$ strand as the fixed
left $\to$ right cut and paste

$R_{k}(X,Y)=X_{1:k}Y_{k+1:5}$ .

With an obligate interior crossover the cut has to lie strictly
inside the five SNP block, $1\le k\le4$, the reciprocal $Y_{1:k}X_{k+1:5}$
being on the $-$ strand and therefore not counted on the $+$ strand
that is being followed.

$F_{1}\to F_{2}$ 
$F_{1}=A/B$.  On the $+$ strand

${\cal G}_{1}=R_{k}(A,B)=0^{k}1^{5-k},\qquad 1\le k\le4$

$01111,00111,00011,00001$,

$|{\cal G}_{1}|=n-1=4$.  In particular every $F_{2}$ chromosome starts
$0$ and ends $1$ and the two founders $00000,11111$ are lost by the
obligate interior crossover.  Up to the fixed orientation this is the
whole $F_{2}$ $+$ strand haplotype pool.

$F_{2}\to F_{3}$ 
Let $h_{i}=0^{i}1^{5-i},\,h_{j}=0^{j}1^{5-j}$, $i,j\in\{1,2,3,4\}$ be
two $F_{2}$ homologues.  On the $+$ strand

$h_{3}=R_{k}(h_{i},h_{j})=h_{i}[1:k]h_{j}[k+1:5]$

satisfies $h_{3,1}=0$ and $h_{3,5}=1$ for every $i,j,k$.  With
$i<k<j$

$h_{3}=0^{i}1^{\,k-i}0^{\,j-k}1^{\,5-j},$

and with $k\le i$ or $k\ge j$ the product is recovered in ${\cal G}_{1}$.

$0\,x_{2}x_{3}x_{4}\,1,\qquad x_{2},x_{3},x_{4}\in\{0,1\}$,

i.e.

${\cal H}_{3}^{+}=\{0x_{2}x_{3}x_{4}1\}$

$00001,00011,00101,00111,01001,01011,01101,01111$,

$|{\cal H}_{3}^{+}|=2^{\,n-2}=2^{3}=8$

distinct $+$ strand chromatids. The four $F_{2}$ molecules are retained
and the four genuinely new two–meiotic molecules are

$01011=R_{2}(01111,00111),\;01001=R_{2}(01111,00001),$
$01101=R_{3}(01111,00111),\;00101=R_{3}(00111,00001)$,

the two founders $00000$ and $11111$ never being recovered with an
obligate $1\le k\le4$ cross.

$|{\cal H}_{3}^{+}|^{2}=8^{2}=64$ ordered maternal/paternal pairs and

unordered diploid $F_{3}$ autosomes on the fixed $+$ strand, the familiar

On the arbitrarily chosen $+$ strand write the two inbred founders as

$P_{0}=0^{5}$ , $P_{1}=1^{5}$

and with the stated strand asymmetry write a meiosis on the $+$ strand as
the fixed left$\to$right cut and paste

$R_{k}(X,Y)=X_{1:k}Y_{k+1:5}\qquad 0\le k\le5$ , 

the reciprocal $Y_{1:k}X_{k+1:5}$ being on the $-$ strand and therefore
not counted on the $+$ strand.  $k=0,5$ is the trivial telomeric cut.

$F_{1}=P_{0}/P_{1}$.  On the $+$ strand

${\cal H}_{2}=R_{k}(P_{0},P_{1})=0^{k}1^{5-k}\qquad0\le k\le5$

is the whole $F_{2}$ haplotype pool.  Up to the fixed orientation the
$F_{2}$ pool is the six monotone $0^{*}1^{*}$ words

$00000,00001,00011,00111,01111,11111,$

the $1^{k}0^{5-k}$ reciprocal products being on the $-$ strand.

An $F_{2}$ individual is $h_{a}/h_{b}$ with $h_{a},h_{b}\in{\cal H}_{2}$,
$h_{a}=0^{a}1^{5-a}$, $h_{b}=0^{b}1^{5-b}$.
An $F_{2}\to F_{3}$ $+$ strand gamete is

$r_{k}(a,b)=h_{a}[1:k]h_{b}[k+1:5]
        =0^{a}1^{\,k-a}0^{\,b-k}1^{\,5-b},\qquad0\le a\le k\le b\le5,$

i.e. a monotone $0^{*}1^{*}$ prefix glued to a monotone $0^{*}1^{*}$
suffix.  Every $F_{3}$ $+$ strand word is therefore a $0^{*}1^{*}0^{*}1^{*}$
word with at most one $1\to0$ step.

* $10=0$: $0^{a}1^{5-a}$, $a=0\ldots5$.  $N_{0}=6$.
* $10=1$ with the unique $1\to0$ at $p$, $1\le p\le4$.  The left $p$ sites
must be $0^{*}1^{*}$ ending in $1$, $0^{a}1^{p-a}$ with $0\le a<p$, $p$
possibilities, and the right $5-p$ sites must be $0^{*}1^{*}$ beginning
in $0$, $0^{c}1^{5-p-c}$ with $0\le c\le5-p$, $5-p$ possibilities.
Hence $N_{p}=p(5-p)$ and

$N_{1}=\sum_{p=1}^{4}p(5-p)=4+6+6+4=20.$

Hence on the fixed $+$ strand

$N_{+}(F_{3})=N_{0}+N_{1}=6+20=26$

different chromatid sequences are attainable, the six monotone words
together with the twenty $0^{*}1^{*}0^{*}1^{*}$ words with a single
$1\to0$.  In diploid terms the $26$ haplotypes can be paired.  There are

$26^{2}=676$ ordered maternal/paternal pairs and

$N_{u}=\binom{26+1}{2}=351$

unordered diploid $F_{3}$ autosomes on the chosen strand.  Words with two
$1\to0$ steps, e.g. $01010$, $10101$, are absent from the $+$ strand
with the one orientation rule; they would need a $1^{*}0^{*}$ block to be
spliced in at the $F_{2}\to F_{3}$ meiosis.

obligatory interior crossover, the two founders are lost in $F_{1}$ and

chromatid is then $0x_{2}x_{3}x_{4}1$ and

${\cal H}_{3}^{+}=\{0x_{2}x_{3}x_{4}1:x_{2},x_{3},x_{4}\in\{0,1\}\}$,

$|{\cal H}_{3}^{+}|=2^{5-2}=8$,

$00001,00011,00101,00111,01001,01011,01101,01111$,

i.e. $8^{2}=64$ ordered and $\binom{8+1}{2}=36$ unordered diploid

limit for two rounds of obligate interior single-crossover meiosis with a
fixed orientation.  This is the $8$ haplotype $36$ genotype limit quoted
under the strict interior $1\le k\le4$ convention. ∎

$$01111,\;00111,\;00011,\;00001,$$

$|{\cal G}_{1}|=n-1=4$ monotone $0^{*}1^{*}$ molecules.  In particular
every $F_{2}$ $+$ strand chromosome starts $0$ and ends $1$ and the two
founder molecules $00000$ and $11111$ are lost by the obligate interior
crossover.  Up to the fixed orientation this is the whole $F_{2}$
haplotype pool.

Let $h_{a}=0^{a}1^{5-a}$, $h_{b}=0^{b}1^{5-b}$ with $a,b\in\{1,2,3,4\}$
be two $F_{2}$ homologues.  An $F_{2}\to F_{3}$ $+$ strand gamete is

$$R_{k}(h_{a},h_{b})=h_{a}[1:k]h_{b}[k+1:5]
      =0^{a}1^{\,k-a}0^{\,b-k}1^{\,5-b},\qquad1\le k\le4,$$

so that

$$R_{k}(h_{a},h_{b})_{1}=0,\qquad R_{k}(h_{a},h_{b})_{5}=1
\;\;\forall\,a,b,k,$$

and with $a<k<b$

$$R_{k}(h_{a},h_{b})=0^{a}1^{k-a}0^{b-k}1^{5-b}.$$

Hence every $F_{3}$ $+$ strand chromatid is of the form $0x_{2}x_{3}x_{4}1$,
the three interior sites being free.  Up to the fixed left $\to$ right
orientation

$${\cal H}_{3}^{+}=\{0x_{2}x_{3}x_{4}1:x_{2},x_{3},x_{4}\in\{0,1\}\}$$

viz.

$$
\begin{array}{llll}
00001,&00011,&00101,&00111,\\
01001,&01011,&01101,&01111,
\end{array}
$$

$|{\cal H}_{3}^{+}|=2^{\,5-2}=2^{3}=8$ different $+$ strand
haplotypes.  The four $F_{2}$ molecules $01111,00111,00011,00001$ are
retained and the four genuinely new two-meiotic mosaics are

$01011=R_{2}(01111,00111),\;01001=R_{2}(01111,00001),$
$01101=R_{3}(01111,00111),\;00101=R_{3}(00111,00001),$

the founder molecules $00000$ and $11111$ never being recoverable with
an obligate $1\le k\le4$ cross.  This is the familiar $2^{\,n-2}$
positive-strand limit for two rounds of obligate single-crossover
meiosis with a fixed orientation.

In diploid terms an $F_{3}$ autosome is an unordered pair
$\{h_{1},h_{2}\}\subset{\cal H}_{3}^{+}$.  There are

$$N_{\rm ord}=|{\cal H}_{3}^{+}|^{2}=8^{2}=64$$

ordered maternal/paternal pairs and

$$N_{\rm u}=\binom{8+1}{2}=36$$

unordered diploid $F_{3}$ $+$ strand autosomes, the $2^{\,n-2}$ 
positive-strand limit.  The $8$ haplotypes are the $0^{*}1^{*}0^{*}1^{*}$
words with the first and last SNP frozen to $0$ and $1$, i.e. at most one
$1\to0$ step on the fixed $+$ strand.

Remark.  If the trivial telomeric cuts $k=0,5$ are formally admitted as
“a crossover’’ the $F_{1}$ $+$ strand pool becomes the six monotone
$0^{a}1^{5-a}$, $0\le a\le5$, words and an $F_{3}$ $+$ strand word is a
$0^{*}1^{*}0^{*}1^{*}$ word with at most one $1\to0$.  Then
$N_{0}=6$ monotone words and $N_{1}=\sum_{p=1}^{4}p(5-p)=20$ words with a
single $1\to0$, i.e. $N_{+}(F_{3})=6+20=26$ distinct $+$ strand
chromatids, $26^{2}=676$ ordered and $26\cdot27/2=351$ unordered
diploid $F_{3}$ autosomes on the chosen strand, the usual
$0^{*}1^{*}0^{*}1^{*}$ textbook repertoire.  The $8$-haplotype,
$36$-unordered-diploid count above is the strict obligate-interior
$1\le k\le4$ fixed-orientation limit. ∎

The + strand convention is decisive and it has to be kept the same in the two meioses.

Put the founders on the chosen + strand as

A = 0⁵ ,  B = 1⁵

and with the stated strand asymmetry write a meiosis on the + strand as the fixed left→right cut and paste

R_k(X,Y)=X[1:k]Y[k+1:5] ,  0 ≤ k ≤ 5 ,

the reciprocal Y[1:k]X[k+1:5] living on the – strand.  The wording
“exactly one locus per generation for every gamete’’ does not force the
locus to fall inside the five SNP interval.  A telomeric cut k=0,5 is still
exactly one crossover per gamete, it is simply telomeric to the block,
and it is the normal textbook way of keeping the founders in the gamete
pool.  With that usual reading

R_k(A,B)=0ᵏ1^{5−k}=h_k ,  0≤k≤5,

so on the + strand

H₂ = {0ᵏ1^{5−k}:0≤k≤5}=00000,00001,00011,00111,01111,11111

is the whole F₁→F₂ gamete pool, |H₂|=6 monotone 0*1* words.  The
1ᵏ0^{5−k} reciprocal products are on the – strand and are therefore not
part of the + strand F₂ pool.  Every F₂ chromosome is h_a/h_b with
h_a,h_b∈H₂.

An F₂→F₃ + strand gamete is

r_k(a,b)=h_a[1:k]h_b[k+1:5]=0^{a}1^{k−a}0^{b−k}1^{5−b},
0≤a≤k≤b≤5,

i.e. a monotone 0*1* prefix glued to a monotone 0*1* suffix.  In
particular an F₃ + strand word can contain at most one 1→0 step.  Let
10(s) be the number of 1→0 transitions.

10=0 : 0^{a}1^{5−a}, a=0…5.  N₀=6.

10=1 with the unique 1→0 at p, 1≤p≤4.  The left p sites have to be a
0*1* word ending in 1, 0^{a}1^{p−a} with 0≤a<p, p choices; the right
5−p sites have to be a 0*1* word beginning in 0, 0^{c}1^{5−p−c} with
0≤c≤5−p, 5−p choices.  Hence

N_p = p(5−p) ,  Σ_{p=1}^{4} p(5−p)=4+6+6+4=20.

Hence on the fixed + strand

N₊(F₃)=N₀+N₁=6+20=26

different chromatid sequences are attainable, the six 0*1* words together
with the twenty 0*1*0*1* words with a single 1→0, e.g.

01011=R₂(01111,00111), 01001=R₂(01111,00001),
01101=R₃(01111,00111), 00101=R₃(00111,00001),

etc.  Words with two 1→0 steps such as 01010,10101 and the four
near-alternating neighbours are absent on the fixed + strand.  They would
require a 1*0* monotone block to be spliced in at the F₂→F₃ meiosis,
i.e. the reciprocal orientation that the stated strand asymmetry removes
from the + strand in the second meiosis.  That is why the 30-haplotype
construction is a double counting of orientations: it re-introduces the
reciprocal 1*0* monotone family on the + strand at the second meiosis.

The strict interior 1≤k≤4 version is the same picture with the
artificial extra convention that a crossover must fall strictly inside the
five SNP block.  With 1≤k≤4 the founders 00000,11111 are lost in F₁ and
every F₃ + strand chromatid is 0x₂x₃x₄1, |H₃⁺|=2^{5−2}=8.  That is a
legitimate pedantic limit, but it is not required by “exactly one locus
per generation for every gamete’’.  Allowing the usual terminal
k=0,5 cuts the founders stay in the pool and the natural + strand F₃
repertoire is the 26 0*1*0*1* set, 26²=676 ordered and 26·27/2=351
unordered diploid F₃ autosomes on the chosen + strand.

On the arbitrarily chosen $+$ strand put

$R_{k}(X,Y)=X_{1:k}Y_{k+1:5}\qquad 1\le k\le4$,

the reciprocal $Y_{1:k}X_{k+1:5}$ being on the $-$ strand and

locus per generation for every gamete’’ is an obligate interior
crossover on the five SNP block, $k=0,5$ is zero recombination and is

$F_{1}\to F_{2}$  

${\cal G}_{1}=R_{k}(A,B)=0^{k}1^{5-k},\;1\le k\le4$,

$R_{k}(h_{i},h_{j})_{1}=0,\qquad R_{k}(h_{i},h_{j})_{5}=1\;\forall i,j,k.$

$00001,00011,00101,00111,$
$01001,01011,01101,01111,$

$|{\cal H}_{3}^{+}|=2^{\,5-2}=2^{3}=8$

different $+$ strand chromatids. The four $F_{2}$ molecules are

orientation.

$\{h_{1},h_{2}\}\subset{\cal H}_{3}^{+}$.  There are
$|{\cal H}_{3}^{+}|^{2}=8^{2}=64$ ordered maternal/paternal pairs and

The four $F_{2}$ molecules are retained and the four genuinely new
two-meiotic mosaics are

$01011=R_{2}(01111,00111),\;01001=R_{2}(01111,00001),$
$01101=R_{3}(01111,00111),\;00101=R_{3}(00111,00001),$

the founders $00000$ and $11111$ never being recovered with an obligate
$1\le k\le4$ cross.

In diploid terms an $F_{3}$ autosome on the chosen strand is an
unordered pair $\{h_{1},h_{2}\}\subset{\cal H}_{3}^{+}$.  There are

$N_{\rm ord}=|{\cal H}_{3}^{+}|^{2}=8^{2}=64$

ordered maternal/paternal pairs and

$N_{u}=\binom{8+1}{2}=36$

unordered diploid $F_{3}$ + strand autosomes, the familiar
$2^{\,n-2}$ positive-strand limit for two rounds of obligate
single-crossover meiosis with a fixed orientation.

Remark.  If the textbook formal convention $k=0,5$ is admitted as a
trivial telomeric cut the $F_{1}{}+$ pool becomes the six monotone
$0^{a}1^{5-a}$, $0\le a\le5$, words.  An $F_{2}\to F_{3}$ + gamete is then
$r_{k}(a,b)=0^{a}1^{k-a}0^{b-k}1^{5-b}$, i.e. a $0^{*}1^{*}0^{*}1^{*}$
word with at most one $1\to0$ step.  There are $N_{0}=6$ monotone words
and $N_{p}=p(5-p)$ words with the unique $1\to0$ at $p$, $N_{1}=
\sum_{p=1}^{4}p(5-p)=20$, so that $N_{+}(F_{3})=6+20=26$ distinct +
strand chromatids, $26^{2}=676$ ordered and $26\cdot27/2=351$
unordered diploid $F_{3}$ genotypes on the chosen strand.  This is the
usual $0^{*}1^{*}0^{*}1^{*}$ $26$-haplotype $351$-genotype count obtained
when the terminal $k=0,5$ cuts are kept in the pool. ∎

12.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: On the arbitrarily chosen + strand let the inbred founders be

A = 00000 ,  B = 11111

and write the asymmetry as a fixed left → right cut-and-paste on the + strand

R_k(X,Y)= X[1:k] Y[k+1:5] , 0 ≤ k ≤ 5,

the reciprocal Y[1:k]X[k+1:5] living on the – strand and therefore not counted on the chosen strand.  That is the operative meaning of “sufficient asymmetry … recombination in only one orientation’’ and “considering only the arbitrarily positive strand’’.

F1 = A/B. On the + strand

H1 = R_k(A,B)=0^k1^{5-k}, 0 ≤ k ≤ 5,

i.e. the six monotone 0*1* words

00000,00001,00011,00111,01111,11111 , |H1|=6,

the 1^k0^{5-k} reciprocals being on the – strand. This is the whole F2 + strand haplotype pool. Every F2 chromosome is h_a/h_b with h_a =0^a1^{5-a}, h_b=0^b1^{5-b} ∈ H1.

An F2 → F3 + strand gamete is

r_k(a,b)=h_a[1:k]h_b[k+1:5]=0^a1^{k-a}0^{b-k}1^{5-b}, 0 ≤ a ≤ k ≤ b ≤ 5,

i.e. a monotone 0*1* prefix glued to a monotone 0*1* suffix. In particular an F3 + strand word can contain at most one 1→0 transition and is of the form 0*1*0*1* with first allele 0 and last allele 1. A second fixed-orientation cut of two 0*1* parents can never create a second 1→0.

10=0 : 0^a1^{5-a}, a=0…5. N0=6.

10=1 with the unique 1→0 at p, 1 ≤ p ≤ 4. The left p sites must be a 0*1* word ending in 1, 0^a1^{p-a}, 0 ≤ a < p, p choices. The right 5-p sites must be a 0*1* word beginning in 0, 0^c1^{5-p-c}, 0 ≤ c ≤ 5-p, 5-p choices. Hence N_p = p(5-p) and

N1 = Σ_{p=1}^{4} p(5-p)=4+6+6+4=20.

Hence on the fixed + strand

N+(F3)= N0+N1 = 6+20 = 26

different chromatid sequences are attainable, the six monotone words together with the twenty 0*1*0*1* words with a single 1→0, e.g.

01011=R2(01111,00111), 01001=R2(01111,00001), 01101=R3(01111,00111), 00101=R3(00111,00001),

etc. Words with two 1→0 steps such as 01010,10101 and the near-alternating neighbours are absent on the fixed + strand; they would require a 1*0* monotone block to be spliced in at the F2→F3 meiosis, i.e. the reciprocal orientation that the strand asymmetry removes from the + strand.

That is why the 30-haplotype construction is a double count of orientations. It re-introduces the 1^k0^{5-k} reciprocal family on the + strand at the second meiosis, effectively allowing both orientations per meiosis. With the one-orientation rule the F2 pool is strictly 0*1* and the second recombination cannot create a second 1→0.

The strict interior 1 ≤ k ≤ 4, 2^{n-2}=8 limit is the same orientation picture with the additional, unnecessary convention that terminal k=0,5 cuts are forbidden. “Exactly one locus per generation for every gamete’’ is normally read with the telomeric intervals admissible, so the founders 00000 and 11111 stay in the F2 pool and the natural + strand F3 repertoire is the 26 0*1*0*1* haplotypes. On the chosen strand that is 26^2=676 ordered and 26·27/2=351 unordered diploid F3 autosomes.

8.text:
On the + strand put the two founders as

$A=0^{5}\;, \; B=1^{5}$ 

and write the meiosis that is seen on the + strand with the stated
strand asymmetry as the fixed left $\to$ right cut and paste

$$R_{k}(X,Y)=X_{1:k}Y_{k+1:5}\;, $$

the reciprocal $Y_{1:k}X_{k+1:5}$ being on the $-$ strand and therefore
not counted on the chosen strand.  With an obligate interior cross the
cut has to lie strictly inside the 5–SNP block,
$1\le k\le 4$, the $k=0,5$ telomeric products being the zero–recombination
gametes.

$F_{1}\to F_{2}$ .  $F_{1}=A/B$ gives on the $+$ strand

$${\cal G}_{1}=R_{k}(A,B)=0^{k}1^{5-k},\qquad 1\le k\le4, $$

$01111,00111,00011,00001,$

$|{\cal G}_{1}|=n-1=4$ monotone $0^{*}1^{*}$ molecules.  In particular
every $F_{2}$ $+$ strand chromatid starts $0$ and ends $1$ and the two
founders $00000,11111$ are lost by the obligate interior crossover. This
is the whole $F_{2}$ $+$ strand haplotype pool up to the fixed
orientation.

Write $h_{a}=0^{a}1^{5-a}$, $h_{b}=0^{b}1^{5-b}$,
$a,b\in\{1,2,3,4\}$, for the $F_{2}$ homologues.  An $F_{2}\to F_{3}$
$+$ strand gamete is

$$R_{k}(h_{a},h_{b})=h_{a}[1:k]h_{b}[k+1:5]
      =0^{a}1^{\,k-a}0^{\,b-k}1^{\,5-b},\qquad1\le k\le4, $$

so that

$$R_{k}(h_{a},h_{b})_{1}=0,\qquad R_{k}(h_{a},h_{b})_{5}=1
\;\;\forall a,b,k,$$

and with $a<k<b$

$$R_{k}(h_{a},h_{b})=0^{a}1^{k-a}0^{\,b-k}1^{\,5-b}.$$

Hence every $F_{3}$ $+$ strand chromatid is of the form
$0x_{2}x_{3}x_{4}1$.  Up to the fixed left $\to$ right orientation

$${\cal H}_{3}^{+}=\{0x_{2}x_{3}x_{4}1:x_{2},x_{3},x_{4}\in\{0,1\}\}, $$

viz.

$$
\begin{array}{llll}
00001,&00011,&00101,&00111,\\
01001,&01011,&01101,&01111,
\end{array}
$$

$|{\cal H}_{3}^{+}|=2^{\,5-2}=2^{3}=8$ different $+$ strand
haplotypes.  The four $F_{2}$ molecules are retained and the four
genuinely new two–meiotic mosaics are
$01011=R_{2}(01111,00111),\;01001=R_{2}(01111,00001),$
$01101=R_{3}(01111,00111),\;00101=R_{3}(00111,00001)$,
the founders $00000,11111$ never being recovered with an obligate
$1\le k\le4$ cross.  This is the familiar $2^{\,n-2}$ positive–strand
limit for two rounds of obligate single–crossover meiosis with a fixed
orientation.

In diploid terms an $F_{3}$ autosome on the chosen strand is an unordered
pair $\{h_{1},h_{2}\}\subset{\cal H}_{3}^{+}$.  There are
$|{\cal H}_{3}^{+}|^{2}=8^{2}=64$ ordered maternal/paternal pairs and

$$N_{u}=\binom{8+1}{2}=36$$

unordered diploid $F_{3}$ $+$ strand autosomes.  With the textbook
convention $k=0\ldots5$ formally admitted the $F_{1}$ $+$ strand pool
becomes the six monotone $0^{a}1^{5-a}$ words and an $F_{3}$ $+$ strand
word is a $0^{*}1^{*}0^{*}1^{*}$ word with at most one $1\to0$ step.
Then $N_{0}=6$ monotone words and $N_{p}=p(5-p)$ words with the unique
$1\to0$ at $p$, $N_{1}=\sum_{p=1}^{4}p(5-p)=20$, i.e. $N_{+}(F_{3})=26$
distinct $+$ strand chromatids, $26^{2}=676$ ordered and
$26\cdot27/2=351$ unordered diploid $F_{3}$ genotypes on the chosen
strand, the usual $0^{*}1^{*}0^{*}1^{*}$ $F_{3}$ repertoire.  This is the
$26$–haplotype, $351$–unordered–diploid count obtained when the
telomeric $k=0,5$ cuts are kept in the pool. ∎

2.text:
On the $+$ strand put

$A=00000\qquad B=11111$

and with the strand asymmetry write the meiosis that is seen on the
$+$ strand as the fixed left $\to$ right cut and paste

$R_{k}(X,Y)=X_{1:k}Y_{k+1:5},\qquad0\le k\le5,$

the reciprocal $Y_{1:k}X_{k+1:5}$ being on the $-$ strand.  Up to the
usual formal telomeric cuts a meiosis is an obligate single cut, $k=0$
and $k=5$ being the $0^{*}$ and $1^{*}$ telomeric cuts.

$F_{1}=A/B$. On the $+$ strand

${\cal H}_{2}^{+}=R_{k}(A,B)=0^{k}1^{5-k},\qquad0\le k\le5,$

i.e. the six monotone $0^{*}1^{*}$ words

$00000,00001,00011,00111,01111,11111,$

$|{\cal H}_{2}^{+}|=6$.  The $1^{k}0^{5-k}$ reciprocals live on the $-$
strand and are not counted on the chosen strand.  Every $F_{2}$
chromosome is $h_{a}/h_{b}$ with $h_{a}=0^{a}1^{5-a}$,
$h_{b}=0^{b}1^{5-b}\in{\cal H}_{2}^{+}$.

An $F_{2}\to F_{3}$ $+$ strand gamete is

$r_{k}(a,b)=h_{a}[1:k]h_{b}[k+1:5]
        =0^{a}1^{\,k-a}0^{\,b-k}1^{\,5-b},
\qquad0\le a\le k\le b\le5,$

a monotone $0^{*}1^{*}$ prefix glued to a monotone $0^{*}1^{*}$ suffix.
Hence every $F_{3}$ $+$ strand word is a $0^{*}1^{*}0^{*}1^{*}$ word
with at most one $1\to0$ step.

* $1\to0=0$ : $0^{a}1^{5-a}$, $a=0\ldots5$, $N_{0}=6$;
* $1\to0=1$ with the unique $1\to0$ at $p$, $1\le p\le4$ :

the left $p$ sites can be any $0^{*}1^{*}$ word ending in $1$, $p$
possibilities $0^{a}1^{p-a},0\le a<p$, and the right $5-p$ sites can be
any $0^{*}1^{*}$ word beginning in $0$, $5-p$ possibilities
$0^{c}1^{5-p-c},0\le c\le5-p$.  Hence $N_{p}=p(5-p)$ and

$N_{1}=\sum_{p=1}^{4}p(5-p)=4+6+6+4=20$.

Hence on the fixed $+$ strand

$N_{+}(F_{3})=N_{0}+N_{1}=6+20=26$

different chromatid sequences are attainable, the six monotone
$0^{*}1^{*}$ words together with the twenty $0^{*}1^{*}0^{*}1^{*}$ words
with a single $1\to0$.  E.g.

$01011=R_{2}(01111,00111),\;01001=R_{2}(01111,00001)$,
$01101=R_{3}(01111,00111),\;00101=R_{3}(00111,00001)$,

etc.  Words with two $1\to0$ steps, $01010,10101\ldots$, are absent
on the fixed $+$ strand; they would require a $1^{*}0^{*}$ block to be
spliced in at $F_{2}\to F_{3}$.

In diploid terms the $26$ $+$ strand haplotypes can be paired.  There
are $26^{2}=676$ ordered maternal/paternal pairs and

$N_{u}=\binom{26+1}{2}=26\cdot27/2=351$

unordered diploid $F_{3}$ autosomal genotypes on the chosen strand.
This is the $0^{*}1^{*}0^{*}1^{*}$ $F_{3}$ repertoire obtained with the
usual textbook $k=0\ldots5$ convention.  With the pedantic strict
interior obligate convention $1\le k\le4$ the two founders are lost in
$F_{1}$, ${\cal H}_{3}^{+}=\{0x_{2}x_{3}x_{4}1\}$,
$|{\cal H}_{3}^{+}|=2^{5-2}=8$, $00001,00011,00101,00111,
01001,01011,01101,01111$, i.e. $8^{2}=64$ ordered and
$\binom{8+1}{2}=36$ unordered diploid $+$ strand $F_{3}$ autosomes, the
familiar $2^{\,n-2}$ positive-strand limit. ∎

4.text:
On the arbitrarily chosen + strand put

A=0^{5}=00000 , B=1^{5}=11111

and with the stated asymmetry write the + strand meiosis as the
fixed left$\to$right cut and paste

$R_{k}(X,Y)=X_{1:k}Y_{k+1:5},\qquad 1\le k\le4$,

the reciprocal $Y_{1:k}X_{k+1:5}$ being on the $-$ strand.  An
obligate interior crossover is required for every gamete, i.e. the
$k=0,5$ telomeric products are excluded by the literal “exactly one
locus per generation for every gamete’’ condition.

$F_{1}\to F_{2}$.  $F_{1}=A/B$ gives on the $+$ strand

${\cal G}_{1}=R_{k}(A,B)=0^{k}1^{5-k},\;1\le k\le4$,

${\cal G}_{1}=\{01111,00111,00011,00001\}$,
$|{\cal G}_{1}|=4=n-1$,
and the two founders $00000,11111$ are lost by the obligate interior
cross.  Every $F_{2}$ $+$ strand chromosome therefore starts with $0$
and ends with $1$.

$F_{2}\to F_{3}$.  Write $h_{a}=0^{a}1^{5-a}$, $a\in\{1,2,3,4\}$ for
the four $F_{2}$ $+$ strand haplotypes.  For $h_{a},h_{b}\in{\cal G}_{1}$

$R_{k}(h_{a},h_{b})=h_{a}[1:k]h_{b}[k+1:5]
      =0^{a}1^{\,k-a}0^{\,b-k}1^{\,5-b},\qquad1\le k\le4,$

so that

$R_{k}(h_{a},h_{b})_{1}=0,\qquad R_{k}(h_{a},h_{b})_{5}=1$

for every $a,b,k$.  Hence every $F_{3}$ $+$ strand chromatid is of the
form $0x_{2}x_{3}x_{4}1$ and the three interior sites are independent
under the fixed left$\to$right orientation.  Up to orientation

${\cal H}_{3}^{+}=\{0x_{2}x_{3}x_{4}1:x_{2},x_{3},x_{4}\in\{0,1\}\}$

i.e.

$00001,00011,00101,00111,$
$01001,01011,01101,01111,$

$|{\cal H}_{3}^{+}|=2^{\,5-2}=2^{3}=8$ different $+$ strand
haplotypes.  The four $F_{2}$ molecules are retained and the four
genuinely new two-meiotic mosaics are

$01011=R_{2}(01111,00111),\;01001=R_{2}(01111,00001),$
$01101=R_{3}(01111,00111),\;00101=R_{3}(00111,00001),$

the founders $00000$ and $11111$ never being recoverable with an
obligate $1\le k\le4$ cross.  This is the $2^{\,n-2}$ positive-strand
limit for two rounds of obligate interior single-crossover meiosis with
a fixed orientation.

In diploid terms an $F_{3}$ $+$ strand autosome is an unordered pair
$\{h_{1},h_{2}\}\subset{\cal H}_{3}^{+}$.  There are

$N_{\rm ord}=|{\cal H}_{3}^{+}|^{2}=8^{2}=64$

ordered maternal/paternal pairs and

$N_{u}=\binom{8+1}{2}=36$

unordered diploid $F_{3}$ $+$ strand autosomes.  The $8$ haplotypes are
the $0^{*}1^{*}0^{*}1^{*}$ words with the first and last SNP frozen to
$0$ and $1$, i.e. at most one $1\to0$ step on the fixed $+$ strand.

Remark.  With the usual textbook convention $0\le k\le5$, i.e. the
telomeric $k=0,5$ cuts are formally admitted as a crossover, the $F_{1}$
$+$ strand pool becomes the six monotone $0^{a}1^{5-a}$ words and an
$F_{3}$ $+$ strand word is a $0^{*}1^{*}0^{*}1^{*}$ word with at most one
$1\to0$ step.  Then $N_{0}=6$, $N_{p}=p(5-p)$ and
$N_{+}(F_{3})=6+\sum_{p=1}^{4}p(5-p)=6+20=26$ distinct $+$ strand
chromatids, $26^{2}=676$ ordered and $26\cdot27/2=351$ unordered diploid
$F_{3}$ autosomes on the chosen strand, the conventional
$0^{*}1^{*}0^{*}1^{*}$ $F_{3}$ repertoire.  The $8$-haplotype,
$36$-unordered-diploid count above is the strict obligate-interior
$1\le k\le4$, fixed-orientation limit required by the literal
exactly-one-interior-locus-per-gamete reading. ∎

$r_{k}(a,b)=h_{a}[1:k]h_{b}[k+1:5]
        =0^{a}1^{\,k-a}0^{\,b-k}1^{\,5-b},
\qquad0\le a\le k\le b\le5,$

a monotone $0^{*}1^{*}$ prefix glued to a monotone $0^{*}1^{*}$ suffix.
Hence every $F_{3}$ $+$ strand word is a $0^{*}1^{*}0^{*}1^{*}$ word
with at most one $1\to0$ step.

* $1\to0=0$ : $0^{a}1^{5-a}$, $a=0\ldots5$, $N_{0}=6$;
* $1\to0=1$ with the unique $1\to0$ at $p$, $1\le p\le4$ :

the left $p$ sites can be any $0^{*}1^{*}$ word ending in $1$, $p$
possibilities $0^{a}1^{p-a},0\le a<p$, and the right $5-p$ sites can be
any $0^{*}1^{*}$ word beginning in $0$, $5-p$ possibilities
$0^{c}1^{5-p-c},0\le c\le5-p$.  Hence $N_{p}=p(5-p)$ and

$N_{1}=\sum_{p=1}^{4}p(5-p)=4+6+6+4=20$.

Hence on the fixed $+$ strand

$N_{+}(F_{3})=N_{0}+N_{1}=6+20=26$

different chromatid sequences are attainable, the six monotone
$0^{*}1^{*}$ words together with the twenty $0^{*}1^{*}0^{*}1^{*}$ words
with a single $1\to0$.  E.g.

$01011=R_{2}(01111,00111),\;01001=R_{2}(01111,00001)$,
$01101=R_{3}(01111,00111),\;00101=R_{3}(00111,00001)$,

etc.  Words with two $1\to0$ steps, $01010,10101\ldots$, are absent
on the fixed $+$ strand; they would require a $1^{*}0^{*}$ block to be
spliced in at $F_{2}\to F_{3}$.

In diploid terms the $26$ $+$ strand haplotypes can be paired.  There
are $26^{2}=676$ ordered maternal/paternal pairs and

$N_{u}=\binom{26+1}{2}=26\cdot27/2=351$

unordered diploid $F_{3}$ autosomal genotypes on the chosen strand.
This is the $0^{*}1^{*}0^{*}1^{*}$ $F_{3}$ repertoire obtained with the
usual textbook $k=0\ldots5$ convention.  With the pedantic strict
interior obligate convention $1\le k\le4$ the two founders are lost in
$F_{1}$, ${\cal H}_{3}^{+}=\{0x_{2}x_{3}x_{4}1\}$,
$|{\cal H}_{3}^{+}|=2^{5-2}=8$, $00001,00011,00101,00111,
01001,01011,01101,01111$, i.e. $8^{2}=64$ ordered and
$\binom{8+1}{2}=36$ unordered diploid $+$ strand $F_{3}$ autosomes, the
familiar $2^{\,n-2}$ positive-strand limit. ∎

On the arbitrarily chosen + strand put

A=0^{5}=00000 , B=1^{5}=11111

and with the stated asymmetry write the + strand meiosis as the
fixed left$\to$right cut and paste

$R_{k}(X,Y)=X_{1:k}Y_{k+1:5},\qquad 1\le k\le4$,

the reciprocal $Y_{1:k}X_{k+1:5}$ being on the $-$ strand.  An
obligate interior crossover is required for every gamete, i.e. the
$k=0,5$ telomeric products are excluded by the literal “exactly one
locus per generation for every gamete’’ condition.

$F_{1}\to F_{2}$.  $F_{1}=A/B$ gives on the $+$ strand

${\cal G}_{1}=R_{k}(A,B)=0^{k}1^{5-k},\;1\le k\le4$,

${\cal G}_{1}=\{01111,00111,00011,00001\}$,
$|{\cal G}_{1}|=4=n-1$,
and the two founders $00000,11111$ are lost by the obligate interior
cross.  Every $F_{2}$ $+$ strand chromosome therefore starts with $0$
and ends with $1$.

$F_{2}\to F_{3}$.  Write $h_{a}=0^{a}1^{5-a}$, $a\in\{1,2,3,4\}$ for
the four $F_{2}$ $+$ strand haplotypes.  For $h_{a},h_{b}\in{\cal G}_{1}$

$R_{k}(h_{a},h_{b})=h_{a}[1:k]h_{b}[k+1:5]
      =0^{a}1^{\,k-a}0^{\,b-k}1^{\,5-b},\qquad1\le k\le4,$

so that

$R_{k}(h_{a},h_{b})_{1}=0,\qquad R_{k}(h_{a},h_{b})_{5}=1$

for every $a,b,k$.  Hence every $F_{3}$ $+$ strand chromatid is of the
form $0x_{2}x_{3}x_{4}1$ and the three interior sites are independent
under the fixed left$\to$right orientation.  Up to orientation

${\cal H}_{3}^{+}=\{0x_{2}x_{3}x_{4}1:x_{2},x_{3},x_{4}\in\{0,1\}\}$

i.e.

$00001,00011,00101,00111,$
$01001,01011,01101,01111,$

$|{\cal H}_{3}^{+}|=2^{\,5-2}=2^{3}=8$ different $+$ strand
haplotypes.  The four $F_{2}$ molecules are retained and the four
genuinely new two-meiotic mosaics are

$01011=R_{2}(01111,00111),\;01001=R_{2}(01111,00001),$
$01101=R_{3}(01111,00111),\;00101=R_{3}(00111,00001),$

the founders $00000$ and $11111$ never being recoverable with an
obligate $1\le k\le4$ cross.  This is the $2^{\,n-2}$ positive-strand
limit for two rounds of obligate interior single-crossover meiosis with
a fixed orientation.

In diploid terms an $F_{3}$ $+$ strand autosome is an unordered pair
$\{h_{1},h_{2}\}\subset{\cal H}_{3}^{+}$.  There are

$N_{\rm ord}=|{\cal H}_{3}^{+}|^{2}=8^{2}=64$

ordered maternal/paternal pairs and

$N_{u}=\binom{8+1}{2}=36$

unordered diploid $F_{3}$ $+$ strand autosomes.  The $8$ haplotypes are
the $0^{*}1^{*}0^{*}1^{*}$ words with the first and last SNP frozen to
$0$ and $1$, i.e. at most one $1\to0$ step on the fixed $+$ strand.

Remark.  With the usual textbook convention $0\le k\le5$, i.e. the
telomeric $k=0,5$ cuts are formally admitted as a crossover, the $F_{1}$
$+$ strand pool becomes the six monotone $0^{a}1^{5-a}$ words and an
$F_{3}$ $+$ strand word is a $0^{*}1^{*}0^{*}1^{*}$ word with at most one
$1\to0$ step.  Then $N_{0}=6$, $N_{p}=p(5-p)$ and
$N_{+}(F_{3})=6+\sum_{p=1}^{4}p(5-p)=6+20=26$ distinct $+$ strand
chromatids, $26^{2}=676$ ordered and $26\cdot27/2=351$ unordered diploid
$F_{3}$ autosomes on the chosen strand, the conventional
$0^{*}1^{*}0^{*}1^{*}$ $F_{3}$ repertoire.  The $8$-haplotype,
$36$-unordered-diploid count above is the strict obligate-interior
$1\le k\le4$, fixed-orientation limit required by the literal
exactly-one-interior-locus-per-gamete reading. ∎
